name: James Clear on creating better habits, systems, goals.
summary: James Clear reviews the main ideas of his book and the concept of developing habits in this long and awesome episode of The Attia Drive. 1. Positive habits see results on the long term (workout) while negative habits are do not have immediate outcome (smoking). In a sense, the cost of bad habits is in the future and the cost of good habits is in the present 2. Behaviors that get immediately rewarded are repeated while those that are immediately punished get avoided; you need relevance and intensity to determine quality of the feedback 3. "Grit is fit": Find your interest 4. It is better to be "process /system" oriented than "outcome" focused 5. If there is a gap between the goals (desired outcome) and the system (collection of daily habits), the system will always win. 6. Types of change Outcome change / Process Change / Identity Change 7. First, identify the identity I want to have and then focus on the process / outcome needed to reach that identity 8. We take upon certain habits as a signal to those around us, not just because of the results they give us. Most people actually choose "belonging" over "outcome" but you need to get balance. 9. The four stages (The Que - something you notice / Craving - the meaning / The Response / The Reward) 10. The laws of behaviour change (one for each phase): Make it obvious, available, easy to see  / make it attractive/ make it easy / make it satisfying. If you want to break a bad habit do the exact opposite  for each phase (don´t buy ice cream) 10. There is not a need (and you will not be) to be perfect but do make sure you correct course ASAP 11. One of the ultimate life skills to an awesome life: Assess where you are in the moment / What is the next step? / define where you want to be / Correct as needed. The optimal would be to reverse engineer from where you want to be. 12. Don´t go all or nothing on your habits; it first needs to "show up" and then improve from there (the 2 minute rule or the guy that went to the gym for 5 minutes) 13. Pick one thing and focus on that; grow from there. Then, optimize the environment (don´t buy ice cream). Gain momentum by rewarding the good and ignore the bad (reinforce the good).

name: Growing Chili Piper´s
summary: Another insightful episode on How To Win with valuable lessons for anybody launching a sport-based SaaS- The main lessons 1. Ask customers for validation of the opportunity you foresee 2. A SaaS needs to embrace "Time to Value" as a key metric 3. People resist change; offer possibility of experimentation 4. Embrace the dark funnel; not everything can or needs to be measure 5. Features are not enough; you need an evalengist and storytelling. 6. Strong retention is how you win; it is not just about acquisition or CRO. The metrics to track are LTV / Net Revenue Retention / Purchasing Frequency 7. Outbeat yourself in innovation to build moats 8. Focus on the process, not the outcome

name: Deep dive into Twitter´s usage metrics
summary: Interesting review of Twitter´s main metrics. What stood out most is that there are huge levels of users in the 16-24 range and, that it is pretty much 10% who Tweet most, while the majority of users "watch."

name: The modern B2B marketing model
summary: Chris Walker shares a few pieces o wisdom on modern B2B marketing frameworks & metrics: 1. Focus on relevance vs awareness 2. Content needs to be value focused vs sales focused 3. Key metrics for marketers: Revenue / Qualified Pipeline / CAC 4. Embrace the "split the funnel" model & sources of opportunity 5. "intent" & "firmographic fit" are the variables that will move to qualified pipeline 6. Nail short term objectives while you build the long term strategy 7. Marketing has to help Sales increase win rate 8. Objectives of first days as CMO (Move qualified pipeline in first 90 days / how can we make something (an event) that helps gather customer insighits (podcast, webinars, etc. / increase direct website traffic

name: How to build "community"
summary: Are you looking to build a strong community? Then this episode of State of Demand of Gen is  "must." The main ideas are: 1. Build around "expertise" & "Engagement" 2. Leverage from dynamics / movements in the market 3. Usually, communities work because they offer professional growth & learning 4. "What is the hook that you offer?" and be sure to niche down 5. Build an audience BEFORE launching the community (Through content and events) and the tech platform may not be as relevant 6. Focus on delivering value for users rather than being a sales channel; the value is by being the most valuable resource 7. Always aim to over-deliver

name: Leveling your Facebook Ads game
summary: This episode of the Social Pros Podcast shares several ideas to level up your marketing game around Facebook ads. The 3 ideas that stood out for us? 1. You need to create different adapts for the different phases of the funnel 2. Creative, targeting and budgeting; you need to understand them well but creative will give you an advantage 3. Test and optimize mentality

name: Is your GTM broken?
summary:
This episode of the Predictable Revenue podcast features Sangram Vajre discussing why most companies fail to scale beyond $10MM in revenue, emphasizing the importance of a robust Go-To-Market (GTM) process. Sangram shares insights from industry leaders and introduces the MOVE framework, highlighting the need for companies to treat GTM as a product and prioritize customer success and RevOps to transition effectively through business stages.

KEY THEMES
• The importance of GTM — GTM is crucial for scaling businesses, yet often overlooked.
• Stages of business growth — Understanding the transitions between problem-market fit, product-market fit, and platform-market fit.
• Role of RevOps — RevOps is essential for moving from product-market fit to platform-market fit.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Only 0.04% of companies scale past $10MM in revenue, primarily due to their GTM process.
• Insight 2: GTM should be owned by the CEO, not just the CMO or CRO.
• Insight 3: The MOVE framework consists of four questions that help businesses mature their GTM process.
• Insight 4: Customer success should be prioritized in the transition to platform-market fit.
• Insight 5: RevOps is crucial for identifying growth opportunities and aligning organizational goals.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• MOVE framework — A set of four questions to guide GTM strategy and ensure it evolves with the business.
• Three stages of company growth — Problem-market fit, product-market fit, and platform-market fit.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Most companies fail because of an unsexy side of business that we don’t talk about enough."
"GTM is the single most important thing that drives business – but we don’t talk about it that way."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Treat your GTM process as a product that needs constant evolution and prioritization.
→ Deploy RevOps as soon as you achieve product-market fit to facilitate the transition to platform-market fit.

name: Leadership lessons from coaching a bad sports team
summary: Insightful episode on The Next Big Idea with leadership lessons coming from the world of high school sports: 1. Be the dumbest guy in the room and make sure you ask for help 2. Hire people who are loyal but that are willing to disagree 3. Make it special by making it hard.  4. Be impatient with behavior but be patient with results 5. Water all your plants and then watch which ones grow 6. Creates layers of leadership: on great teams, everybody leads.

name: Web design best practices vs standardrs
summary: Andy Crestodina shares some great research that compares what  the web design "standard" says you shoudl do vs the  13"best practices" you can apply to actually build a fantastic website.

name: Master guide on building the marketing funnel
summary: Are you looking to take your marketing funnel to the next level? Read this awesome article on CXL that gives a detailed explanation and examples for each phase of the funnel. They finish off the article with four business metrics you need to track and optimize: Cost per acquisition (CPA) / LTV / Conversion Rate / Conversion Rate per Source. We are pretty sure it can help you nail your marketing strategy.

name: Create impact through messaging by making customers feel smart, capable and good
summary: Insightful episode of The Social Media Examiner Podcast which shares tangible advice on developing a messaging strategy that creates impact on customers: 1. First, understand who your customer really is vs the one you wish they were 2. Focus on getting customers to take action vs on customer needs. 3. "At their core, most people want to feel smart, capable, and good. Every decision they make is geared toward achieving one of these three states of mind" (The example on the "weight loss" brand is also applicable to sport...) 4. Implement a framework (Understand your audience / What are the goals they want to achieve? / What needs to be true so they can consider your offer? / Anticipate the problem that needs to be solved / Change their perspective without making them feel "not good, not smart, not capable"

name: Peloton is pushing through resistance
summary: They consider themselves a media business, tt stands out they are platform agnostics (it is not about just streaming in their platform).

name: The Refine Labs marketing framework & Why it is the best time to be a B2B marketer
summary: Another awesome episode of State of Demand Gen with many good ideas to keep in mind: 1. The best marketers have certain experience in Brand, Demand Gen, Product Marketing & Field. They also have a deep understanding of their audience 2. They understand there are two types of customers ("In Market" vs "Not in Market") 3.They quantify impact in a way that the CEO / CFO can understand using revenue related metrics ( Growth rate / CAC / Pipeline velocity / competitive advantage / Cost per opportunity source) 4. Their process towards positioning is Segmenting the market / Targeting (Learn to say no to certain customers) / Positioning / Messaging. 5 Dig deep into types of customers when segmenting (Recurring revenue model / High margin / High Growth / Multistakeholder sale / Business model / Budget / Funding / Organizational Structure)

name: Wilson´s marketing strategy around racket sports (In Spanish)
summary: Interesting review of how Wilson carries out its marketing strategy in Europe, the rise of padel, etc. Their objectives are: 1. Drive people to their website and increase sales from there 2. Engage in social 3. Ensure brand image among D2C players such as Tennis Point

name: State of SEO industry
summary:
This episode discusses the State of SEO 2021 Report as a case study for using surveys in content marketing to generate leads and build brand awareness. Shelley Walsh and Loren Baker explore the strategies and challenges involved in creating impactful surveys, emphasizing the importance of unique data and audience building.

KEY THEMES
• Survey as a Marketing Tool — Using surveys to generate leads and build brand authority.
• Audience Building — The significance of creating and leveraging your own audience for sustained engagement.
• Content Repurposing — Strategies for effectively repurposing content to maximize reach and impact.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Surveys can serve as powerful tools for lead generation and establishing industry authority.
• Insight 2: Unique data from surveys can naturally attract backlinks and media coverage.
• Insight 3: Building your own audience, such as an email list, provides long-term value and control.
• Insight 4: Drip feeding and repurposing content in various formats enhances brand building.
• Insight 5: Small businesses can focus on qualitative data and use cost-effective methods like Twitter polls.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Gated Content — Content that requires users to provide information before accessing, used to generate leads.
• Drip Feeding — Gradually releasing content to maintain audience engagement over time.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Having unique data is always a real plus point, and one of the real benefits of it is the fact that they are natural linking machines. –Shelley Walsh"
"If you’ve done a study or survey the first time, don’t give up. By continuously doing it, people start to expect it, and it starts to grow. –Loren Baker"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider using surveys as a strategy to generate leads and enhance brand authority.
→ Build and maintain your own audience, such as an email list, for long-term engagement and insights.

name: Lochhead on Facebook´s rebrand to Meta
summary:
In this episode, Christopher Lochhead discusses Facebook's rebranding to Meta and the launch of a new category, the metaverse. He explores the strategic brilliance and the significant issues surrounding this move, questioning whether it was a legendary act of category design or a misstep due to unresolved trust issues and a lack of mission-driven purpose.

KEY THEMES
• Rebranding Strategy — The strategic implications of Facebook's rebranding to Meta and its attempt to create a new category.
• Category Design — The importance of tying a company's name to its category for long-term success.
• Trust and Reputation — The challenges Facebook faces due to its reputation and lack of trust among users.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Facebook's rebranding to Meta is unprecedented for a trillion-dollar company launching a forward-leaning category.
• Insight 2: Tying a company name to its category can provide staying power within that category.
• Insight 3: Ignoring existing trust issues and controversies can undermine a company's strategic moves.
• Insight 4: Legendary category designers are mission-driven, aiming to make a difference beyond economic success.
• Insight 5: Facebook's presentation of the Metaverse focused more on the company's benefits rather than user-centric solutions.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Category Design — A strategic approach where a company creates and dominates a new market category.
• Mercenary vs. Missionary — A concept contrasting profit-driven motives with purpose-driven innovation.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Whatever you want to say about Zuckerberg, what he pulled off there was legendary and by the book, at least from a purely category design perspective."
"Zuckerberg’s announcement made it clear that he’s a mercenary, not a missionary."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider the importance of addressing trust issues when launching new products or rebranding.
→ Evaluate whether your company's strategic moves are mission-driven and solve real problems for users.

name: Review of Facebook´s Q3 2021 results & their rebrand to Meta
summary: Interesting revenue stats for Facebook and their take on thei rebrand to Meta

name: Pat Flynn on The Remarkable People Podcast
summary: Pat Flynn reviews his career, lessons learned and gives advice to build a side project in an actionable way.

name: Messaging as your "go-to punch"!
summary:
This episode features Alexandra Gutow, Director of Product Marketing Management at Snowflake, discussing the critical role of messaging in product marketing. The conversation explores how effective messaging can enhance the go-to-market (GTM) process and win deals by crisply articulating the unique aspects of a product.

KEY THEMES
• The importance of messaging in product marketing — Messaging is crucial for creating a strong market impression and aligning internal teams.
• The dynamic nature of messaging — Messaging is a continuous process that requires testing and refinement.
• Career insights in product marketing — Insights into the career path and current outlook for product marketing professionals.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Messaging is a living process that requires constant testing and refinement.
• Insight 2: Internal alignment across the organization is crucial for effective messaging.
• Insight 3: Crisply articulating the unique aspects of a product is key to a successful GTM process.
• Insight 4: Effective messaging can significantly impact the success of winning deals.
• Insight 5: Product marketing is a promising career path with opportunities for growth and impact.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Messaging frameworks — Tools and strategies that help articulate product uniqueness and enhance GTM effectiveness.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Messaging is a living breathing process that when done right, equates to an impactful impression left on your market."
"Crisply articulating the unique aspects of your product that you’re bringing to market is key to the success of your GTM process!"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Continuously test and refine your messaging to ensure it remains effective.
→ Ensure strong internal alignment within your organization to support effective messaging.

name: The future of broadcasting and digital in the Bundesliga
summary:
Andreas Heyden, CEO of DFL Digital Sports, joins SportsPro managing director Nick Meacham to discuss the innovation and production behind the Bundesliga.
Launched almost ten years ago, DFL Digital Sports is a subsidiary of the Bundesliga with the objective of driving all of the German soccer league's production and innovation as a media business.
Andreas has been with the organisation more than six years, and is always one of the smartest people in the room. In this podcast, we dig into the Bundesliga's OTT strategy, how it uses data, works with tech startups and is driving a new fan experience through a range of innovations being rolled out across its channels.

name: The modern leader "brings it" & leads with empathy
summary:
This episode features Chris Capossela, Microsoft's CMO, discussing his leadership style and career journey. He emphasizes leading with empathy, empowering teams, and balancing personal growth with organizational goals. His insights are rooted in his upbringing in a family-run restaurant and his extensive experience at Microsoft.

KEY THEMES
• Empathetic Leadership — Chris highlights the importance of empowering others and leading with empathy.
• Balancing Personal and Professional Growth — Chris discusses the need to balance learning with performance and personal fulfillment with corporate goals.
• Adapting to Change — The episode explores how companies, including Microsoft, are adapting to new work environments and employee expectations.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Chris believes in giving the stage to others, similar to how a restaurant operates successfully when everyone works together.
• Insight 2: His upbringing in a family restaurant instilled a strong work ethic and prepared him for a multifaceted career.
• Insight 3: Chris emphasizes the importance of balancing inspiration with accountability and learning with performing.
• Insight 4: He learned the value of aligning company goals with societal needs and employee desires.
• Insight 5: Chris is excited about the shift towards flexible work environments, which can attract diverse talent.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Empathetic Leadership — Leading by empowering others and focusing on collective success.
• Balancing Contradictions — Managing the tension between performance and learning, accountability and inspiration.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""The restaurant only works if everybody works together.""
""You have to use Microsoft as your platform, to do what matters to you.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Leaders should focus on empowering their teams and giving others the stage.
→ Organizations should align their goals with societal needs and employee aspirations to retain talent.

name: CRO and digitization in a catering & rural hotel business (In Spanish)
summary: Sometimes, the basics (understanding your audience and meeting them where they are) are enough to "crush" it. Simple yet insightful business case on how a traditional business embraced digital tech.

name: How to set marketing growth goals
summary: To set goals, you need to play with two variables: Net new business & Average Revenue per Customer; this is the topic of this episode on the Actionable Marketing Podcast. To define our objectives, we need to think about creating quality leads on one hand and on the other, do not dismiss the opportunities of growing revenue from your existing customer base (cross selling).Also, be aggresive, if you never failed it means you never tried hard enough (when that happens, consider explaining what happened, why, and what are you are going to do to fix it); at the end of the day, it is about learning. Keep in mind that the ultimate goal should be revenue, so  all KPIs should be oriented towards achieving revenue and your goals set with that frame in mind.

name: The content value curve
summary:
This episode explores the concept of the content value curve, which distinguishes between tactical and strategic content in marketing. It emphasizes the importance of focusing content on either tactical or strategic value to effectively reach different audiences and achieve specific marketing goals.

KEY THEMES
• Content Value Curve — Differentiates between tactical and strategic content and their respective audiences.
• Tactical vs Strategic Content — Explains the inverse relationship between tactical and strategic content value.
• Content Strategy — Highlights the importance of aligning content with marketing goals and audience needs.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Content should focus on providing either tactical or strategic value, not both.
• Insight 2: Tactical content is situationally relevant and helps solve specific problems but lacks broad appeal.
• Insight 3: Strategic content provides new frameworks or perspectives and can enhance brand perception.
• Insight 4: An effective content strategy includes a mix of tactical and strategic content tailored to different stages of the marketing funnel.
• Insight 5: The choice between tactical and strategic content should be guided by marketing goals, target audience, and industry maturity.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Content Value Curve — A framework that maps content based on its strategic or tactical value.
• Counter-narrative Thought Leadership — Content that challenges industry norms and provides strategic insights.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""For a piece of content to be successful, it must avoid trying to fulfill multiple objectives for its audience.""
""Tactical and strategic content speak to radically different audiences.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Focus content on providing either tactical or strategic value to avoid diluting its effectiveness.
→ Align content strategy with specific marketing goals and the maturity of the industry.

name: Searching for happiness (In Spanish)
summary:
This episode explores the concept of 'the opposite of loneliness,' inspired by Marina Keegan's reflections on connection and community. It delves into the importance of human relationships and the fear of losing the sense of belonging, emphasizing that happiness is deeply tied to our connections with others.

KEY THEMES
• The Opposite of Loneliness — The episode discusses the elusive feeling of connection and community that is not quite love or friendship but a sense of belonging.
• Youth and Possibility — Emphasizes the potential and opportunities available to young people, encouraging them to embrace change and new beginnings.
• Fear of Missing Out — Explores the anxiety of not living up to one's potential and the fear of being left behind by peers.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The opposite of loneliness is a profound sense of belonging and community.
• Insight 2: The fear of losing one's community can be more daunting than career or relationship concerns.
• Insight 3: The best years of our lives are not behind us; they are part of us and can be recreated.
• Insight 4: Young people often feel pressured by impossibly high standards and the fear of falling behind.
• Insight 5: It is crucial to retain a sense of possibility and openness to change throughout life.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• The Opposite of Loneliness — A concept describing a deep sense of belonging and community.
• Youth and Possibility — The idea that young people have the time and opportunity to change and explore.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"We don't have a word for the opposite of loneliness, but if we did, I would say that's what I want in life."
"The best years of our lives are not behind us. They are part of us and will repeat as we grow."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Embrace the sense of community and belonging wherever you find it.
→ Remember that it's never too late to start anew or change your path.

name: Behind the scenes with Capti
summary:
This episode features Jeff Veldhuizen, CEO of Capti, discussing the innovative aspects of Capti's game-based smart bike. The conversation highlights how Capti is revolutionizing at-home fitness by integrating immersive gaming experiences and exploring the potential of fitness in the metaverse. Jeff shares insights on the convergence of fitness, wellness, and healthcare and its implications for business and culture.

KEY THEMES
• Innovation in Fitness Technology — Capti's unique approach to combining gaming with fitness.
• The Metaverse and Fitness — Exploring the future of fitness in virtual worlds.
• Convergence of Health Sectors — How fitness, wellness, and healthcare are merging.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Capti offers a dual-mode bike that can switch between a road bike and a studio bike using Smart Ride™ technology.
• Insight 2: The bike's immersive gaming experience sets it apart from other connected fitness equipment.
• Insight 3: Capti aims to power fitness experiences in the metaverse, expanding the boundaries of traditional fitness.
• Insight 4: Jeff Veldhuizen has a background in growing major brands like Nike and Zwift, bringing valuable experience to Capti.
• Insight 5: The convergence of fitness, wellness, and healthcare presents new opportunities for business innovation and cultural impact.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Smart Ride™ technology — Allows Capti's bike to morph between different modes for versatile fitness experiences.
• Fitness in the Metaverse — Concept of integrating fitness activities into virtual worlds for enhanced engagement.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Capti delivers adventure, exploration, and discovery through virtual worlds."
"A smarter way to track the future of health."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore the potential of integrating gaming elements into fitness products to enhance user engagement.
→ Consider the implications of the metaverse for future fitness and wellness offerings.

name: Why & how sport properties can embrace the fight against climate change
summary: Be prepared, think green, take action (take small steps). This framework comes from this brilliant episode on Sports Pro Media that shares actionable advice for sport properties to embrace climate change. Why should you care? Well, climate changes drives heatwaves, droughts and other natural phenomena that impact the ability to carry out competitions normally. In essence, 80%-90% of sport´s emissions come from "energy," "transport" & "food so what can brands do to take action? Among other things: 1. Set reduction targets 2. Reduce or change travel behaviors (plane vs bus) 3. Incentivize fans to adopt different transport patterns through discounts or merch 4. Foster suppliers and partners to embrace the fight (This could even mean changing the approach towards sponsorship...)

name: Goldman Sachs on Consumer Retail Trends & IPOs
summary:
This episode discusses the surge in IPOs within the consumer retail sector, focusing on companies that produce everyday goods. Host Allison Nathan interviews Jennifer Davis and Vishaal Rana from Goldman Sachs' Consumer Retail Group to explore why these companies are attracting investor interest.

KEY THEMES
• IPO Market Trends — Examination of the current record-setting IPO market.
• Consumer Goods Popularity — Analysis of why consumer goods companies are appealing to investors.
• Investment Strategies — Insights into how investors are approaching the consumer retail sector.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The IPO market is experiencing a record-setting period, particularly for consumer goods companies.
• Insight 2: Investors are showing strong enthusiasm for companies that produce everyday items.
• Insight 3: Consumer retail companies are leveraging public offerings to capitalize on market trends.
• Insight 4: The consumer retail sector is seen as a stable investment due to its essential nature.
• Insight 5: Companies in this sector are using IPOs to expand their market presence and drive growth.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• IPO Market Dynamics — Understanding the factors driving the current surge in IPOs.
• Consumer Retail Investment — Strategies for investing in the consumer goods sector.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Investors are enthusiastic about consumer goods and services."
"The makers of things we use in our everyday lives are standing out in the IPO market."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider investing in consumer goods companies going public to capitalize on current market trends.
→ Analyze the stability and growth potential of consumer retail companies as part of an investment strategy.

name: Lessons on "focus" & "pivoting" from Privy
summary: The main lessons from this one: Listen to customers and their pain points to see if you need to pivot your business. A freemium model is great to help customers solve their use case prior to paying for the solution. Identify your area of focus, your specific target and delive against their needs relentlesly.

name: Winning the marketing game with storytelling
summary:
Kathleen Booth interviews Postie co-founder and CEO David Fink on the Inbound Success podcast and they discuss why combining a mission driven brand message with deep authenticity is the key to win.
Everything needs to start with the "Why" but emphasizing that it needs to come from authenticity. They then go on share a few examples of brands that are doing this correctly, including some from the world of sport!

name: Decoding greatness: Becoming legendary by evolving from the lessons of others
summary: In order to decode greatness, there is a stigma that says that you either need to be naturally talented or practice your 10K hour. However, on this episode of Christopher Lochhead´s "Follow your different" they share how the legends actually reversed engineered what other greats before them did. There is a magic line between emulating them and using them as inspiration to develop your awesome work. This could be combining uniqueness from different sources (influences) (Derivative with a twist as Don Draper said). There are other methods such as "reverse outlining" which is basically unpacking what makes something great but then make sure you evolve it. The key is to figure out what works in a different field and look for opportunities to apply it to yours and make it authentic to you. They also discuss tips for startups such as the value of "selling" first and "building" later as a means to test the market beforehand. Confirm that what you are building is directionally correct and that people are willing to pay for it rather than being perfect from the get-go. This will help you validate the idea sooner and better.

name: Opportunities for sport apparel brands in the metaverse: Virtual goods, "Brand" or "Manufacturing" as a service and leveraging the best from both worlds
summary: This article shared by Wunderman Thompson is a must for those of you in the sport apparel industry. They interview Aglet´s founder & CEO and he discusses how we approaches the development of the business model in the metaverse, the need to embrace a virtual and physical component or how small and big brands can work together in partnership to achieve growth.

name: What Startup founders can learn from Moderna
summary: The future is designed, not predicted. This and more awesome lessons can be learned in this fantastic episode of Starting Greatness through the lens of Moderna´s CEO. Other "nuggets" include: 1. Play offense with risk . This harness first mover advantages 2. Use back-casting to predict risky futures with massive upside; it assumes a very radical future and works backwards from there. It is based on thought experiments (vs empiric) and contemplates 3 different futures (plausible, possible & preposterous) 3. Determine your future-founder fit: Which risky future is best for you and your team? 4. You must connect the future with the present (What needs to happen so this can happen?) and move people towards that future you foresee 5. "Vision without execution is just hallucination."

name: The impact of stopping advertising, positioning vs differentiation and growing through acquisition vs loyalty
summary: Research: 1. Advertising helps maintain sales, not necessarily grow; in essence it is a defensive tactic that if nudged correctly, it can create a nudge to buy the brand among those exposed to the ad. 2. Big brands are more protected than smaller brands 3. Brands share customers with each other in line with brand size (Duplication of purchase law) 4. If a brands wants to grow, you need scale / market penetration; positioning matters less. 5. Positioning impacts in the short term. In the long term, you do need differentiation 6. Review of the Double Jeopardy Law: Focus on acquisition to fight it, not loyalty. 7. Focus in increasing physical and mental availability

name: The best lessons from 100 episodes of Masters of Scale
summary: This episode of Masters of Scales is packed with awesome advice for startup founders: 1. Starting a business is hard at the personal level (stress, loneliness, etc.) so being very resilient is critical 2. Embrace being small, focus on building a product so amazing that customers will tell others about it. 3. Trust within the team determines how fast you can move (Truly a team sport, right?)

name: Advertising successfully to Gen Z
summary:
This episode explores the growth of digital advertising, focusing on mobile ad spending and the shifting landscape of TV ad dollars. It also delves into Gen Z's advertising preferences and the future of Apple Podcasts' in-app subscriptions, providing insights into current advertising trends and strategies.

KEY THEMES
• Digital Advertising Growth — Analyzing the factors contributing to the increase in digital ad spending.
• Mobile Ad Spending — Discussing the potential limits of mobile ad spending's market share.
• Gen Z Preferences — Understanding how Gen Z interacts with and prefers advertising.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Digital advertising is experiencing significant growth, driven by various factors.
• Insight 2: Mobile ad spending is increasing, but there may be a ceiling to its market share.
• Insight 3: TV ad dollars might be declining as digital platforms gain prominence.
• Insight 4: Gen Z has distinct preferences for how they engage with advertisements.
• Insight 5: Apple Podcasts' in-app subscriptions could influence podcast monetization strategies.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Brand & Performance Integration — The idea of merging brand building and performance marketing into a single strategy.
• The Funnel Collapse — A concept describing the shortening of the consumer journey from click to purchase.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“It’s time to stop thinking about brand & performance separately.”"
"“With an hour between click & doorstep, the funnel has collapsed.”"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider integrating brand and performance marketing strategies to adapt to the collapsing funnel.
→ Explore the potential of in-app subscriptions on platforms like Apple Podcasts for new monetization avenues.

name: Customer insights must drive marketing strategy & the most overrated channels
summary: Being customer centric is actually about understanding customers problems, delivering content they need (vs the one you want them to need). The best way to develop your marketing strategy is by talking to them, interviewing them, touch upon they things they value most (overall, not in reference to your product), finding their truth (not yours) and then obtaining insights from those conversations. Chris Walker also shares the most overrated channels (Paid Search ads, Trade booths & sponsorship of events, LinkedIn Lead Gen, Head count (?), Gated content syndication, martech). inally, they have an interesting conversation around creating ambassadors for your product, which should actually be thought of something that happens thanks to the quality of your product beforehand and then, enhancing their role as ambassadors

name: Sail GP & the role of sustainability in creating competitive advantage
summary:
Competitive advantage, says Porter, can be derived from two main sources: doing things at lower cost or differentiation.
Sustainability has been touted as a form of differentiation – but if every organisation needs to get their environmental house in order to align with emerging policy and public opinion, how can organisations differentiate on these grounds?
In his own Harvard Business Review article from 2019, one of this week’s guests, Ioannis Ioannou, puts forward the argument that while sustainability can be competitive advantage for some, this will only extend to the organisations going beyond risk management and embedding sustainability in their organisational strategy, leading to new innovation in products and services that provide solutions for consumers and the planet.
SailGP is one of the handful of sports properties to have sustainability as a key pillar of its strategy and operations. Its mantra, ‘powered by nature’, reflects this. And even though its ambitious net zero carbon strategy (2025) and focus on sustainable development in host cities has won the attention of fans and partners like Tesla, its chief executive Sir Russell Coutts insists that this is not to carve out a competitive advantage – but to be in-step with other leading organisations.
In this podcast, Coutts and Fiona Morgan, SailGP’s director of purpose and impact, follow up on Ioannou’s observations by showcasing their approach to social and environmental leadership, which includes establishing an innovative approach to athlete engagement and competition in the shape of the Impact League.

name: Unbundling the creator economy
summary: (In Spanish) THis episode reviews what the creator economy is, the future opportunities, the challenges, how involving your audience is key for growth, etc

name: The marketing playbook that works in B2B
summary: Chris Walker shares a few thoughts on marketing in B2B today including: 1. adapting to the way customers buy 2. The playbook to follow (have a point of view, communicate it in a way the audience like & distribute the info your audience wants in the platforms that matter - social networks, communities, word of mouth, content platforms) 3. Find channels with high reach & high upside and focus on that! Then expand 4. The channels to explore: Events, content platforms, distribution in the most prominent social networks (LinkedIn, FB, Podcast, YouTube and Tik Tok in the future)  5. Your thought experts should be someone with a similar background a your audience 6. In B2C there is no sales team, so your marketing should sell stuff 7. The difference between Creating Demand vs Capturing Demand and why you should educate the market

name: Exploring the frontiers of Web 3 & NFTs
summary: Awesome conversation that helps understand what Web 3 is, the opportunities, the risks, the regulation, trying to climb different mountains. It is a deep conversation that fundamentally tackles the way it should be approached. In essence, it should not be about adapting web 2 to web 3; web 3 needs to be tackled with a beginners mind....They even discuss Sorare, so check it out as it touches the world of sport

name: Instagram testing new tools for creators: Partnership folders
summary:
If you work in sports or fitness, we are pretty sure this tool that Instagram is testing out will be of interest. As Sam Carp from Sports Pro summarizes:  Creators can add participating brands they’re interested in working with, which gives them priority when brands are searching for endorsers
A new ‘partnership messages’ folder will be added within Instagram DMs where sponsors and creators can manage their branded content partnerships
Data and unique filters are now available for brands to discover creators best suited to their campaigns. It is not fully clear sports will be included in the test, but logic would seem, based on the audience there, it will.

name: Masterclass for those in the fitness industry: The $500 challenge & the value equation
summary:
In this episode, Alex Homozi, Founder and CEO of Acquisitions.com, shares insights into creating irresistible offers and building profitable gyms. He discusses his book $100M Offers, the value equation, and his approach to entrepreneurship and philanthropy. The conversation provides valuable lessons on risk-taking, wealth-building, and systematic problem-solving.

KEY THEMES
• Creating Irresistible Offers — Alex discusses how to craft offers that customers can't refuse.
• Value Equation — Understanding the four key variables that create value for customers.
• Entrepreneurship and Philanthropy — Alex's journey in business and his commitment to reinvesting in altruistic initiatives.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Alex Homozi emphasizes the importance of creating offers so compelling that people feel foolish saying no.
• Insight 2: The value equation consists of four key variables that determine the value for the customer.
• Insight 3: Systematic problem-solving can be enhanced by interviewing experts, a technique Alex learned from management consulting.
• Insight 4: Alex's success in the fitness industry is rooted in a step-by-step guide to building profitable gyms.
• Insight 5: Alex and his wife Leila's partnership has been crucial in their successful business ventures.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Value Equation — A framework consisting of four key variables that create customer value.
• $100M Offers — A concept from Alex's book about making offers so good that they are irresistible.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Alex Homozi: 'Make offers so good people feel stupid saying no.'"
"Alex Homozi: 'It's my duty to reinvest my wealth into altruistic initiatives.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider how you can apply the value equation to enhance the offers you present to customers.
→ Explore systematic problem-solving by consulting with experts in your industry.

name: The future of Demand Gens depends on buyer led content marketing
summary:
This episode explores the future of demand generation, emphasizing the importance of buyer-led content marketing. It highlights how AI and content governance play crucial roles in shaping brand identity and ensuring content authenticity in the zero-click era, making it essential for marketers to adapt their strategies accordingly.

KEY THEMES
• AI as a Gatekeeper — AI engines are now critical in determining brand visibility and identity.
• Content Governance — Ensuring content authenticity and alignment with brand identity in the zero-click era.
• Buyer-Led Content Marketing — Shifting focus to content that is driven by buyer needs and preferences.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• AI engines are the new gatekeepers to brand identity, influencing how content is perceived and accessed.
• Content governance is essential to maintain authenticity and control over brand representation.
• The zero-click era requires marketers to adapt strategies to ensure content is engaging and accessible.
• Overlooked content assets can be pivotal in driving acquisition success.
• AI is reshaping content and marketing roles, creating a 'ghost workforce' that influences job markets.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• CRISP Framework — A method for preparing content for agentic AI.
• Trust Lattice Framework — A model for measuring content marketing trust in the AI age.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"AI engines are the new gatekeepers to your brand."
"Content governance is one of the biggest tools to ensure they reveal the brand identity you’ve created."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement content governance strategies to maintain brand authenticity.
→ Leverage overlooked content assets to enhance acquisition efforts.

name: How to sell & promote your products on Instagram Live
summary: 1. Choose a topic for the stream 2. Promote the stream 3. Give a short into 4. Pin a post and ask for the audience to share it 5. Change the pinned post and the CTA during the stream 6. Define your final CTA and introduce your next Instagram live

name: Ariel Helwani: Building his own ESPN
summary:
In this episode, Ariel Helwani discusses his decision to leave ESPN and pursue an independent career in the MMA industry. He shares insights on how he structures his business, the importance of choosing a niche, and the benefits of embracing controversy to build a strong personal brand and audience.

KEY THEMES
• Independence in Media — Ariel's transition from ESPN to building his own brand
• Niche Markets — The advantages of focusing on a specific area like MMA
• Controversy as a Tool — How engaging with controversial topics can enhance audience engagement

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Ariel Helwani left ESPN to gain more control over his career and content.
• Insight 2: He structures his business to drive revenue through multiple channels, including YouTube and Substack.
• Insight 3: Ariel chose to focus on MMA because it was an underserved niche with passionate fans.
• Insight 4: He gives away his Substack revenue as a strategy to build a loyal audience.
• Insight 5: Embracing controversy can be a powerful way to engage and grow an audience.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Niches Get Riches — The idea that focusing on a specific niche can lead to greater success.
• Leaning into Controversy — Using controversial topics to drive engagement and audience growth.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Niches get riches.""
""Leaning into controversy can be a powerful way to engage and grow an audience.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider focusing on a niche market to build a strong, dedicated audience.
→ Explore ways to engage with controversial topics to increase audience engagement.

name: Using "opportunity per source" to understand sales velocity pipeline
summary: Chris Walker shares 3 main ideas on this one: 1. Tik Tok is for those on "offense" 2. Sales velocity pipeline metrics (win rates, conversion rates, sales cycle lenght) and how you should match those agains "opportunity source 3. You need to build credibility beforehand to make the sales process quicker

name: Behind the scenes: La Liga Tech
summary: Nice review (in Spanish) of La Liga Tech´s business model (tech to improve fan engagement, the competition and protect its content) and the opportunities they foresee. This includes, offering their platform to other sport properties locally and internationally

name: Embracing AR through Snapchat
summary: The CMO of Snap gives more details on how brands can embrace (and must!) embrace AR within their marketing strategy in this episode of CMO Moves. These include "try-ons" or making the shopping experience entertaining.  This is an exponential technology so marketers would do well in starting exploring it...

name: SEO Masterclass: The Google Ranking Factors
summary:
This episode of the Search Engine Journal Show features a discussion with Anna Crowe and Loren Baker about Google ranking factors, aiming to separate fact from fiction. The conversation revolves around their ebook 'Google Ranking Factors: Fact or Fiction,' which seeks to clarify misconceptions and provide factual insights into what truly influences search engine rankings.

KEY THEMES
• Debunking SEO Myths — The episode focuses on distinguishing between confirmed Google ranking factors and common misconceptions.
• User Experience in SEO — Emphasizes the importance of creating a better user experience as the ultimate goal of SEO strategies.
• Research-Driven Insights — Highlights the extensive research process behind the ebook to ensure the accuracy of information.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The ebook 'Google Ranking Factors: Fact or Fiction' took nearly two years to compile, emphasizing the importance of thorough research.
• Insight 2: Google ranking factors are often misunderstood, with many myths circulating in the SEO community.
• Insight 3: User intent satisfaction is a key focus for Google when ranking search results.
• Insight 4: Content freshness is a confirmed ranking factor, underscoring the need to keep content updated and relevant.
• Insight 5: Links, particularly contextual and inbound links, are significant ranking factors, while others like nofollow links are not.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Google Ranking Factors: Fact or Fiction — An ebook that aims to clarify what is and isn't a Google ranking factor.
• Query Deserves Freshness — A concept that suggests content freshness can affect website rankings.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"The more you understand how the Google algorithm works, the better you can deliver an amazing piece of content to the user. — Anna Crowe"
"It’s about science, so it’s interesting to learn how the algorithm works. But it’s more important to realize that the goal really is to build a better page for the user. — Anna Crowe"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Focus on satisfying user intent with your content to improve search rankings.
→ Regularly update your content to maintain its relevance and value, as freshness is a confirmed ranking factor.

name: When marketing legends get together: Seth Godin on the Remarkable People Podcast
summary: Remarkable episode with Guy Kawasaki interviewing Seth Godin in a conversation full of wisdom for any marketer out there: 1. Marketing is not advertising, it is doing generous work that matters for people who care, and making a change FOR them and WITH them. All of it is a story of who the customers believes they are when they interact with our brand 2. The internet is about what people say about when they talk about you; the network effect is far more powerful than advertising. 3. Review the concept of the minimum viable audience; your true true fans 4. Mediocre stuff is hard to charge a premium for & make something that the right people think is great and worth talking about 5. Marketing is about making a change in the world that makes you proud (don´t be slave to metrics)

name: Hacking Growth
summary:
Growth is now the first thing that investors, shareholders and market analysts look for in assessing and valuing companies.
HACKING GROWTH is a highly accessible, practical, method for growth that involves cross-functional teams and continuous testing and iteration. Hacking Growth does for marketshare growth what THE LEAN STARTUP does for product development and BUSINESS MODEL GENERATION does for strategy. HACKING GROWTH focuses on customers - how to attain them, retain them, engage them, and monetize them - rather than product.
Written by the method's pioneers, this book is a comprehensive toolkit or "bible" that any company in any industry can use to implement their own Growth Hacking strategy, from how to set up and run growth teams, to how to identify and test growth levers, and how to evaluate and act on the results. It is designed for any company or leader looking to break out of the ruts of traditional marketing and become more collaborative, less wasteful, and achieve more consistent, replicable, and data-driven results.

name: A course on "Personal branding"
summary: Personal branding is about understanding "who you are / what you do / how you do it."

name: The most important marketing equation
summary:
This episode of Lochhead on Marketing discusses the critical equation in business and marketing: 'Results do not equal No Results plus an Excuse.' Christopher Lochhead emphasizes the importance of results in defining one's reputation and success, particularly in competitive fields like marketing and category design.

KEY THEMES
• The importance of results in business — Results are the primary measure of success and reputation.
• Excuses vs. accountability — Excuses can perpetuate a lack of accountability and hinder success.
• Category design and market leadership — In any category, there is typically one dominant leader capturing the majority of the market.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Results are the foundation of your reputation in business.
• Insight 2: Excuses can become a mindset that prevents achieving desired outcomes.
• Insight 3: In marketing and category design, being the category leader is crucial for capturing market share.
• Insight 4: Clear goals are essential in marketing to avoid wasting time and resources.
• Insight 5: Legendary figures in business are those who consistently produce results, regardless of circumstances.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Results do not equal No Results plus an Excuse — A principle emphasizing the importance of results over excuses.
• Category King/Queen — The concept of a market leader who dominates a category by capturing the majority of the market share.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Results do not equal No Results plus an Excuse."
"You are your results and your results drive your reputation."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Train yourself to focus on producing results rather than making excuses.
→ Ensure clarity of marketing goals within your team to optimize efforts and resources.

name: Owning the PMM Craft
summary:
In this episode, Pallavi Vanacharla, Head of Product Marketing Management (PMM) for IoT at Twilio, discusses her journey in marketing and her insights into leading a PMM team. She shares her perspective on the 80/20 rule, team structuring, and the importance of happiness in achieving company success. This episode is valuable for understanding effective product marketing strategies and leadership in a growing company.

KEY THEMES
• Career Path in Product Marketing — Pallavi's journey and evolution in the marketing field.
• Team Structuring and Coordination — Insights on organizing and aligning a product marketing team with company goals.
• Leadership and Company Success — The role of happiness and management in driving company success.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Pallavi emphasizes the importance of evolving one's role in marketing to lead all functions effectively.
• Insight 2: The 80/20 rule is crucial in prioritizing tasks and focusing on what truly drives impact.
• Insight 3: Structuring a product marketing team requires clear coordination with PMs and other groups to align goals.
• Insight 4: Success measurement involves setting tailored goals for team members at different levels.
• Insight 5: Happiness and effective management are critical for the overall success of a company.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• 80/20 Rule — Focus on the 20% of work that drives 80% of the results.
• Team Structuring — Organizing a team to align with company goals and coordinate with other departments.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""The success of the company depends on the manager.""
""Happiness is a critical component of achieving company success.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Apply the 80/20 rule to prioritize tasks that have the most significant impact.
→ Structure your team to ensure clear coordination and alignment with other departments.

name: Fighting the continuum
summary: We live in a world obsessed by categorizing everything and when it comes to people, it is hard to change the first impression. But we are people, we can evolve, we can improve...we are a continuum. Granted we may not become NBA superstars, but we are destined to become better, if we put the effort and the hours behind it.

name: The 365 laws of Mastery with Robert Greene
summary: A two part episode on the James Altucher show that can "shake your foundations." Robert Greene discusses his pursuit of mastery, even if you feel like "it´s too late for you." Some of the lessons you will find in there include: - It´s OK to pursue a fulfilling career; it helps you connect with yourself and therefore, with others. - Accept your weirdness, it makes you unique - Mastery is a process that takes years (have short term goals that lead to your long term objective) - With all the information at our disposable, the power in the world in the future is to connect several ideas together - Don´t try to please others all the time - Don´t listen too  much to what others have to say; do not underestimate your innervoice - Your level of excitment determines so much of what happens to you - Look to connect the dots of all your past experiences - Find out where the position of energy and momentum lies

name: Jim Nantz: The man behind the voice
summary:
This episode features a conversation with Jim Nantz, a renowned American sportscaster known for his work with CBS Sports. Jim shares his journey in broadcasting, his struggles with anxiety, and the techniques he used to overcome it. The discussion highlights his commitment to authenticity, joy, and storytelling in sports broadcasting.

KEY THEMES
• Overcoming Anxiety — Jim discusses his early career struggles with anxiety and how he used deliberate practice and imagery to overcome it.
• Authenticity in Broadcasting — Jim emphasizes the importance of being conversational and authentic rather than scripted in his broadcasts.
• Joy and Passion for Sports — Jim expresses his deep joy and passion for sports, which he aims to convey in his broadcasts.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Jim Nantz struggled with anxiety early in his career and used deliberate practice and imagery to overcome it.
• Insight 2: He values authenticity in broadcasting, preferring a conversational style over a scripted one.
• Insight 3: Jim's voice is often praised, and he attributes it to his father, whom he admired greatly.
• Insight 4: He keeps a meticulous log of his activities to better understand and improve himself.
• Insight 5: Jim views his role as a 'paid observer,' focusing on the stories and emotions of the athletes he covers.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Deliberate Practice — Jim used this approach to overcome anxiety by visualizing and preparing for various scenarios.
• Paid Observer — Jim describes his broadcasting role as observing and conveying the stories and emotions of athletes.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Joy is something that’s real. It’s in your soul. It’s in your core. It’s who you are.""
""I’m a paid observer. They pay me to observe a sporting event and tell people at home what it is that I see.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Listeners could apply deliberate practice and imagery to overcome personal challenges.
→ Embrace authenticity in communication, focusing on being genuine rather than perfect.

name: Trying to understand the potential of AI w/ Eric Schmidt
summary: If you are interested in the uses of AI and, most of all, how it can impact our daily lives, the politics around it and what could we see in the future, this episode is a "must. " We particularly liked his description of AI in 4 traits: Innacurate / Dynamic / Unexpected / Learning

name: Positioning masterclass & Pitching your point of view w/ April Dunford
summary: Your buyers have more choices than ever. And only focusing on your product doesn’t make it any easier on them. April Dunford, Founder of Ambient Strategy and Author of Obviously Awesome, will give you the full rundown on why you need to develop a point of view narrative. So you can give your prospects and customers a better (and more clear) way to think about their choices in a crowded market.

name: Embracing constructive conflict to grow your business
summary: Interesting views and lessons from Ray Dalio on how embracing conflict (in a constructive manner) leads to the growth of the business. Self knowledge & trust are key to harness conflict in a positive way. Let go of the ego.

name: Nike´s Sport Research & Innovation Lab
summary: Explains the different ways in which they help everyday athletes improve performance through their technology

name: Level up your Tik Tok with these 8 examples
summary: Tik Tok is, arguably, one of the platforms with most potential for brands in the future, and in our opinion, it is a platform pretty much "made" for the sport industry. If you are looking to level up your Tik Tok game, then check out this Hubspot article which shares 8 brands that are "winning" on Tik Tok, including the NBA and one of our favorites, Gymshark.

name: State of the podcasting industry
summary:
This episode discusses the global state of the podcasting industry, highlighting insights from a comprehensive forecast by eMarketer. It explores podcast penetration across 18 major markets, emphasizing the influence of language on podcast adoption and the growing prominence of Spanish as a podcasting language.

KEY THEMES
• Global Podcast Penetration — Analysis of podcast listener forecasts across 18 major markets.
• Language and Podcast Adoption — The impact of language on the accessibility and popularity of podcasts.
• Emerging Spanish-Language Market — The rise of Spanish as a significant language in the podcasting industry.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Podcasts are becoming a borderless medium, yet language remains a significant barrier to global adoption.
• Insight 2: The US leads in both podcast content production and listener adoption due to its vast English-language library.
• Insight 3: Countries with high English proficiency have higher podcast adoption rates.
• Insight 4: Non-English speaking countries like Japan, South Korea, France, Germany, and Italy have lower podcast adoption.
• Insight 5: Spanish is emerging as a second universal language for podcasting, with significant growth in Spanish-speaking populations.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Podcast Penetration Forecast — A comprehensive set of international forecasts for podcast listeners developed by eMarketer.
• Language Barrier in Podcasting — The concept that language understanding is crucial for podcast enjoyment and adoption.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Podcasts are an increasingly borderless medium."
"Spanish is well on the way to becoming the second universal language for podcasting."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider producing content in multiple languages to reach a broader audience.
→ Explore opportunities in the growing Spanish-language podcast market.

name: Marketing lessons from Seth Godin
summary:
This episode focuses on Louis Grenier's consultancy, Stand The F*ck Out, which specializes in helping B2B companies find and amplify their unique market positioning. The discussion highlights the importance of differentiating in a crowded market and offers insights into effective marketing strategies that cut through noise, particularly in the age of AI.

KEY THEMES
• Differentiation in Marketing — Finding what makes a company stand out in a crowded market.
• AI and Marketing — Using AI to amplify unique brand positioning.
• Consultancy Approach — Short, intense sprints instead of long-term retainers for more effective results.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Many B2B companies struggle to showcase their unique strengths due to being too close to their business.
• Insight 2: Traditional marketing playbooks often lead to comfortable but stagnant growth.
• Insight 3: Short, intense consultancy engagements can be more effective than long-term retainers.
• Insight 4: A clear differentiation and narrative design are crucial for effective market positioning.
• Insight 5: AI can be leveraged to amplify a company's unique positioning and reach.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Stand The F*ck Canvas — A one-page document that articulates what makes a company different and why people should care.
• Content Matrix & Narrative — A system to maintain authentic and engaging content without running out of ideas.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""You can't see the label when you're inside the jar." — David C. Baker"
""Life's too short to build a business you hate, and too precious to market with bullshit." — Louis Grenier"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Conduct a gap analysis to identify and articulate your unique market positioning.
→ Implement a content matrix to ensure consistent and authentic brand communication.

name: Making sponsorship strategy simpler with Sponsorpulse
summary: The Halftime Snacks podcast publishes an interesting overview of Sponsorpulse, one of the companies looking to make a splash in the sport sponsorship landscape. The episode cover how their service works or the potential use cases of the software.

name: Behind the scenes with On-Running: A premium sport apparel brand rooted sustainability and a suscription-based business model
summary:
This episode features Marc Maurer, co-CEO of On, discussing the company's IPO and growth strategies in retail and direct-to-consumer channels. The conversation highlights On's unique blend of performance, design, and sustainability in the sports apparel market, and explores the convergence of fitness, wellness, and healthcare and its implications for business and culture.

KEY THEMES
• IPO and Growth Strategies — Exploring On's recent IPO and its impact on retail and direct-to-consumer growth.
• Performance and Sustainability — How On differentiates itself through a commitment to performance and sustainable design.
• Convergence of Sectors — The merging of fitness, wellness, and healthcare and its broader implications.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: On's IPO presents new growth opportunities in both retail and direct-to-consumer markets.
• Insight 2: The integration of performance, design, and sustainability is key to On's market differentiation.
• Insight 3: On's mission is to ignite the human spirit through movement, aligning with broader wellness trends.
• Insight 4: The convergence of fitness, wellness, and healthcare is reshaping business strategies and consumer expectations.
• Insight 5: On's strategic focus includes leveraging sustainability as a core component of its brand identity.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Convergence of Fitness, Wellness, and Healthcare — This concept explores how these sectors are merging and impacting business strategies.
• Direct-to-Consumer Growth Strategy — A focus on expanding direct sales channels to enhance customer engagement and brand loyalty.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Marc Maurer: 'Our mission is to ignite the human spirit through movement.'"
"Marc Maurer: 'Combining performance, design, and sustainability is how we stand out in a crowded market.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore direct-to-consumer channels to enhance customer engagement and drive growth.
→ Incorporate sustainability into product design and brand messaging to differentiate in the market.

name: Understanding Europe´s fiscal policy and political situation across countries
summary: Good to understand the current state of Europe´s fiscal & political situation

name: Pensamiento Liminal: Expandiendo nuestras fronteras
summary:
This episode explores the concept of 'liminal thinking' and how expanding our perspectives can lead to breakthroughs in understanding and problem-solving. Using the metaphor of the blind men and the elephant, it highlights how our limited experiences shape our perceptions and how shifting these can reveal a more complete picture.

KEY THEMES
• Perception and Reality — Our understanding is limited by our experiences, similar to the blind men and the elephant.
• Liminal Thinking — The practice of expanding and redefining our mental models to gain new insights.
• Breakthrough Moments — How changing perspectives can lead to sudden solutions and discoveries.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Our perceptions are limited by our personal experiences, much like the blind men's understanding of the elephant.
• Insight 2: Breakthroughs often occur when we expand or redefine our mental models.
• Insight 3: Liminal thinking involves intentionally shifting perspectives to provoke new insights.
• Insight 4: Waiting for insights to happen by chance is less effective than actively seeking new perspectives.
• Insight 5: Understanding the full picture requires acknowledging the limitations of our current viewpoint.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Liminal Thinking — A method of expanding and redefining mental models to gain new insights.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Each of us is blind in our own way, describing the world based on our experience."
"We build our models of the elephant based only on what we have been able to touch."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Practice liminal thinking by actively seeking new perspectives and challenging your current mental models.
→ Reflect on areas where your understanding might be limited and explore different viewpoints to gain a fuller picture.

name: Learning from the best: How Manchester United uses its digital platforms to engage with fans worldwide
summary: If you want to take your sport business to the next level, it always helps to understand how the best in the business are "winning." This is why we believe this episode of StreamTime, in which they review how Manchester United is engaging with fans across all digital channels (social media, app, eCommerce, etc.) can be of great value. They discuss the value of understanding well your fan base, the role of segmentation, personalizing the experience through the nationalities of the players or "Level of fandom", how they embrace the "brand strength" of different players, efforts to monetize from a worldwide fan base and some opportunities for the future, including attacking "the middle" (which refers to activating and engaging those worldwide fans that may not have the chance to experience a life game)

name: What growth marketing really is and the  tactics you can use to implement it across the AARRR framework
summary:
This episode provides a comprehensive guide to growth marketing, distinguishing it from traditional marketing and growth hacking. It emphasizes the importance of a strategic, evidence-based approach to long-term goals, focusing on acquisition, retention, and cross-selling. The episode also explores the AARRR framework, detailing strategies and metrics for each stage of the growth marketing funnel.

KEY THEMES
• Growth Marketing vs Traditional Marketing — Growth marketing is strategy-based with long-term goals, unlike traditional marketing which is campaign-oriented and short-term.
• Growth Marketing vs Growth Hacking — Growth hacking focuses on short-term results, while growth marketing looks at the bigger picture with sustainable strategies.
• AARRR Framework — This popular framework, also known as the Pirate Funnel, outlines stages and metrics for growth marketing.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Growth marketing focuses on long-term goals and evidence-based planning, unlike traditional marketing which is short-term and opinion-based.
• Insight 2: Cross-selling and upselling can increase order value and reduce acquisition costs in e-commerce.
• Insight 3: Growth hacking can achieve quick results through experimentation, as seen in Dropbox's referral program.
• Insight 4: The AARRR framework divides growth strategies into acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and revenue stages.
• Insight 5: Personalization and customer experience are crucial for retention, as 80% of customers prefer brands that offer personalized experiences.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• AARRR Framework — A five-stage framework for growth marketing focusing on acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and revenue.
• Pirate Funnel — Another name for the AARRR framework, emphasizing its structured approach to growth strategies.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Growth marketing is more than just a buzzword for growing businesses. It’s a well-devised plan for sustainable progress and taking your business to greater heights."
"The rule of thumb for boosting revenue is to triple your customer lifetime value against the acquisition costs."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement cross-selling and upselling strategies to increase order value and reduce acquisition costs.
→ Use personalization technology to enhance customer experience and build loyalty.
→ Create a referral program to leverage loyal customers for brand promotion.

name: Winning at Inbound
summary: Great episode on Inbound Success for those interested in winning the inbound game. Many lessons you can apply to your own strategy: 1. Obsess about customers and their problems rather than on products & features 2. Embrace a variety of channels to intervene in.This means participating across several platforms to generate touchpoints and new audiences 3. Increase frequency of posting but being mindful of the central message you want to transmit; don´t spam 4. Be agile (Don´t over think it). Overall, you need to maintain an obligation to the deliver the best possible content possible and be ready to play the long time.

name: "How to win" with Shopify´s VP of Growth
summary: Awesome episode on "How to Win" with lessons from Shopify on staying ahead of the competition, which can help any sport business out there. Some of the main lessons are 1. Spotify relies on making it very easy and accessible to enter their platform (they pursue "volume" rather than "margin" but be careful with competing for customers based on low cost / prices, this attract less quality customers. 2. To win in messaging you need a clear brand identity, a robust positioning (what use case do you solve?) and 3 capabilities: Know what the people you serve want, copy writing skills & Know that what you are saying is landing on your target market (message testing). 3. Strategic growth starts with an honest assessment of where you are, then define where you want to be in a year which will help you define a gap, the obstacles in your way, define initiatives to cover an obstacles (careful with mistaking obstacles with symptoms). 4. If you want to go after the category leader, you need to define a new "where to play box" and not go directly after the exact same market. 5. The best companies assume they will not be "winning" forever, which pushes their boundaries to improve constantly.

name: Behind the scenes with an NBA Refereer
summary: He talks with Steve about being scrutinized by players, fans, and management; how much work — and data — go into being fair; and why he talks about race with his colleagues and his kids.

name: Trends across media platforms
summary:
This episode explores significant trends in the media landscape, focusing on the rise of smart products, the stagnation of social media usage, and the evolving use of voice assistants. Experts Jason Mander and Karin von Abrams provide insights into these developments and their implications for the industry.

KEY THEMES
• Rise of Smart Products — Exploring how smart products are becoming more integrated into daily life.
• Social Media Plateau — Examining the implications of stagnant growth in social media usage.
• Voice Assistant Utilization — Investigating the diverse ways people are using voice assistants.

• Insight 2: The plateau in social media usage suggests a saturation point may have been reached.
• Insight 3: Voice assistants are being used in more varied ways, indicating a shift in user interaction with technology.
• Insight 4: The media landscape is rapidly evolving with technological advancements.
• Insight 5: Understanding these trends is crucial for businesses to adapt their strategies accordingly.

"Jason Mander: 'Smart products are not just a trend; they're becoming a staple in consumer lifestyles.'"
"Karin von Abrams: 'The plateau in social media usage could signal a need for platforms to innovate.'"

→ Marketers need to consider new strategies to engage users as social media growth plateaus.

name: How to use Snapchat in your marketing campaigns
summary: For some reason, we believe Snapchat has the potential to become one of the predominant social media platforms in the not so distant future, particularly for sport apparel brands out there. If you feel the same, then you cannot miss this episode of The Search Engine Journal Show where they discuss the potential Snapchat brings to brands. There are 5 primary realms Snapchat can be used for marketing (Media Planning / Competitive Research / Market research / Copywriting / Develop Customer Personas) but the biggest potential comes in the use of Augmented Reality, which can be used across the entire funnel in 3 ways: 1. Communicate 2. Utility 3. Entertainment. Image recognition is particularly useful for sport apparel brands as their technology even helps people find their perfect size for a particular item without having to visit the store or guess, which ultimately is of great benefits for brands as they avoid "return-related" costs that usually drain huge margins.

Research & insights on the audience 2. Develop a strategy / a point of view 3. Decide on the content and the format 4. Distribute the content. name: Deeper into the metaverse, Metacast & the D2Avatar model in Roblox
summary:
This episode delves into the evolving concept of the metaverse, highlighting its potential impact on technology, sports, and entertainment. It explores how major tech companies like Facebook, Epic Games, and Unity are investing in virtual and augmented reality to create immersive digital experiences, and discusses the implications for brands and industries as they develop metaverse strategies.

KEY THEMES
• The Metaverse Vision — Exploration of how companies are conceptualizing and investing in the metaverse as a successor to the internet.
• Technological Innovations — Discussion of advancements in AR, VR, and volumetric capture that are shaping the metaverse.
• Economic and Strategic Implications — Analysis of how brands and industries are preparing for a future where digital and physical worlds converge.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Major tech companies are investing heavily in the metaverse, with Facebook repositioning itself as a 'metaverse company' and Epic Games securing significant funding to build social experiences.
• Insight 2: Unity's Metacast uses volumetric capture to create interactive 3D sports and entertainment experiences, enhancing both viewer engagement and professional analysis.
• Insight 3: The metaverse is expected to offer unprecedented interoperability, allowing digital items to move seamlessly across different virtual environments.
• Insight 4: Roblox exemplifies a thriving metaverse platform, with its D2A (Direct to Avatar) model allowing users to purchase virtual goods for their avatars.
• Insight 5: NFTs are emerging as a way to secure digital transactions within the metaverse, creating trust and facilitating a digital economy.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Metaverse: A collective virtual shared space, created by the convergence of virtually enhanced physical reality and physically persistent virtual space.
• D2A (Direct to Avatar) Model: A business model where consumers purchase digital goods for their avatars in virtual environments.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“If the last generation is about sharing, the next generation of social is going to be about participating.” — Sima Sistani"
"“Every brand will need a metaverse strategy in the future and the ones that have them now are at the forefront.” — Christina Wootton"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Brands should start developing a metaverse strategy to stay ahead in the evolving digital landscape.
→ Explore partnerships with platforms like Roblox to create immersive brand experiences and engage with digital communities.

name: The basics of RFM Analysis and how it can level up your marketing game
summary: The Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM) method is a great way to segment your current customer base as it enables you to tailor your offering to their actual behaviors. This article on Sendpulse explains the basics of the RFM analysis with examples, the benefits and the "how-to."
