name: NFT & Web 3.0 will drive "community-led" built communities
summary:
The next evolution of companies will be created in public with early customers, partners, and supporters. They’ll be community-owned and operated, building upon the playbooks created by early NFT and play-to-earn projects. Because many of the web 3.0 advantages are hard to adopt as a large web 2.0 company, as a Founder you have to focus on the big ideas: ownership, collaboration, and community.
In today's episode, NFX Partner Morgan Beller talks with Cuy Sheffield (head of crypto at Visa) and Micah Johnson (Bored Apes, CryptoPunks, and Aku and former professional baseball player) as they explore tactics for building community, no matter what industry you’re in. name: Media is the new marketing w/ Joe Pulizzi
summary:
In this episode, Joe Pulizzi discusses the evolving landscape of media marketing, emphasizing the importance of networking and strategic partnerships over isolated efforts. He also shares insights on focusing content creation efforts and outlines a seven-step process to build an online audience capable of generating multiple revenue streams.

KEY THEMES
• Networking over Isolation — Emphasizing collaboration and partnerships to expand audience reach.
• Focused Content Creation — Advocating for niche content strategies rather than trying to be everywhere.
• Building Revenue Streams — Steps to develop an online audience that can generate income.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Networking and partnerships can help reach a larger audience than isolated efforts.
• Insight 2: Creating content for the sake of content is ineffective; focus on niche areas where you can excel.
• Insight 3: A walled garden approach limits audience growth potential.
• Insight 4: The seven steps to building an online audience can be applied with any budget.
• Insight 5: Strategic content placement is more impactful than trying to be present on all platforms.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Seven Steps to Build an Online Audience: A process outlined by Joe Pulizzi for creating multiple revenue streams.
• Walled Garden Approach: A strategy that limits audience growth by isolating content.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Rather than fighting with organizations with the same audience as yours, believe in the power of networking."
"Trying to be present everywhere and creating content for the sake of content both get a big, big thumbs down."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Focus your content efforts on niche areas where you can make a significant impact.
→ Consider forming partnerships and collaborations to expand your audience reach.

name: Building the most sustainable city
summary: Since stepping down as Walmart’s president of e-commerce at the beginning of the year, billionaire entrepreneur Marc Lore has had a busy year of big ideas. In the Spring, it was announced that he reached a deal to purchase the NBA’s Minnesota Timberwolves and the WNBA’s Minnesota Lynx, alongside Alex Rodriguez. And then last month, he outlined his plans to build a new American city called Telosa, centered around sustainability and inclusion. Lore, who co-founded Jet.com, an e-commerce company that sold to Walmart in 2016, says that he approaches these moonshot ideas in the same manner: by reverting to the fundamentals and naming the mission and values. "VCP: vision, capital, people,” he says. “If you get VCP right, everything else falls in place." It stands out that he is learning to play basketball without a ball! It is foundational, which also can transalte to business

name: Where & how to add "social proof" on your website
summary:
This episode explores the concept of social proof and its critical role in enhancing the credibility and performance of web pages. It discusses various types of social proof, such as testimonials, endorsements, and data, and provides practical advice on how to effectively integrate them into website design to build trust and influence potential customers.

KEY THEMES
• Importance of Social Proof — Social proof is essential for building credibility and trust on web pages.
• Visual Hierarchy — Proper placement and prominence of social proof elements are crucial for their effectiveness.
• Types of Social Proof — Different forms, including testimonials, endorsements, and data, can be leveraged to enhance web page performance.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Social proof is not the main reason visitors come to a website, but it is crucial for building trust and credibility once they are there.
• Insight 2: Testimonials should be prominently displayed on popular pages rather than hidden on less-visited pages.
• Insight 3: Endorsements from trusted individuals or media can transfer credibility to your brand, known as the Halo Effect.
• Insight 4: Data and statistics, when related to your work, can serve as powerful social proof.
• Insight 5: Social media metrics can backfire if they show low engagement, leading to negative social proof.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Halo Effect — A psychological phenomenon where the endorsement from a trusted individual or entity transfers credibility to your brand.
• Visual Hierarchy — The arrangement of elements on a page to guide the viewer's attention to the most important information, such as social proof.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Quotation marks are the most powerful key on your keyboard.""
""Your customer is a better messenger for many of your most important messages.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Ensure social proof elements are easy to spot by placing them high in the visual hierarchy of your web pages.
→ Use analytics to identify your most popular pages and ensure they feature your strongest social proof elements.

name: "brand tracking:" The metrics that matter and the "how-to"
summary:
If you want to get a sense of the power of your brand, this guide published on CXL´s blog is a great start. It offers explanations on the metrics that matter (NPS & CSAT, Brand Loyalty, Brand Awareness & Brand Usage), examples and what we liked most, real questions you can use to asses the impact your brand has in the market.            NPS & CSAT
NPS – On a scale from 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend [your company] to a [friend/family member/colleague]?
CSAT – On a scale from 1 to 5, how would you rate your experience at [your company] today?
Brand loyalty
On a scale from 0 to 10, how likely are you to purchase [product] form us again?
For how long have you been buying [your product]?
On a scale from 0 to 10, how likely are you to switch to a competing product in the future?
Brand usage
When was the last time you used [your product]?
How often do you use [your product]?
Do you use our products exclusively, or do you switch between brands?
Why is that?
What do you use [your product] for? (for more comprehensive offerings such as software packages)
When you purchase [X product] how often do you buy [your product]?
Don’t get too complicated with these questions. Customers should be able to answer from top of mind and too much cognitive effort tends to lead to less reliable answers.
Brand awareness
When you think of [X product or service], what brands come to mind?”
If they mention your brand: “What stands out to you about our brand and why?”
If they mention another brand: “What stands out to you about [competitor brand] and why?”
Have you heard of [your brand] before?
On a scale from 1 to 10, how familiar are you with [your brand]?
Which of the following brands have you heard of? (list your own + competitors)

name: Detailed guide to Facebook marketing strategy, building communities & advertising
summary:
Fantastic article on CXL´s blog going into the steps & tactics to build your Facebook marketing strategy. First, they describe 5 elements your Facebook strategy needs:
1.	Defined audience
2.	Strong goals

4.	Established voice
5.	Consistent tracking and measuring

It has it all!

name: Being purpose driven & prioritizing wellbeing to attract and retain top talent
summary:
This episode discusses the importance of being purpose-driven and prioritizing well-being in sports organizations to attract and retain top talent. It highlights the need for new approaches and thinking to address key people themes in the industry, such as creating a collaborative culture and leveraging technology.

KEY THEMES
• Attracting and Retaining Talent — Focus on hiring the right talent and developing diverse teams.
• Modern Culture and Leadership — Creating collaborative and cross-generational work environments.
• Technological Change — Supporting employees in leveraging technology to enhance capabilities.

MAIN INSIGHTS

• Insight 2: Developing diverse teams with a real voice is crucial for business success.
• Insight 3: Creating flatter, collaborative organizations can motivate a cross-generational workforce.

• Insight 5: Supporting employees in using the latest technology can augment their capabilities.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS

• People Agenda — A focus on putting people at the heart of sports business.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Putting people at the heart of the business of sport requires a new focus, new thinking, and new approaches."
"How do we build and maintain diverse teams of people with a real voice that contributes to the success of business?"

summary: Interesting view on the sectors that this VC focuses on (performance; sports and gaming; media and fan engagement; as well as data analytics and monetisation). What stood out most is her belief that the "metaverse" is here

name: Developing a career as PMM
summary:
This episode features Naman Khan, CMO at Zeplin, discussing the evolving role of product marketing managers (PMMs) and how individuals can develop their careers in this field. The conversation highlights the increasing recognition of product marketing in organizations and offers insights into career advancement strategies, including leveraging personal strengths and continuous learning.

KEY THEMES
• The evolving recognition of product marketing — Companies are increasingly valuing product marketing roles.
• Career development strategies — Importance of identifying strengths and areas for improvement.
• The role of kindness in professional success — Being nice can significantly impact career growth.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Product marketing roles are becoming more prevalent as organizations recognize their value.
• Insight 2: Staying updated with market trends is crucial for career advancement in product marketing.
• Insight 3: Applying the 80/20 rule to focus on strengths and areas for development can lead to career success.
• Insight 4: Kindness and being a nice person are powerful tools for professional growth.
• Insight 5: Continuous learning and adapting to new trends are essential for maintaining and excelling in a PMM role.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• 80/20 rule — Focus on the 20% of activities that yield 80% of the results in personal and professional development.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Never underestimate the power of kindness and being a nice person."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Identify your strengths and areas for improvement to apply the 80/20 rule in your career development.
→ Stay informed about market trends to remain competitive in the product marketing field.

name: Behind the scenes with Dux Gaming
summary: (In Spanish) A behind the scenes looks at DUX gaming, their model combining traditional sports with eSports, their plans in the NBA, how they got there, etc.

name: A rant on LTV vs CAC for sport businesses

In essence, increasing LTV can be done by generating multiple revenue streams and they give a bunch of examples of players in the industry that are doing so.

name: Invest in content as much as distribution, the role of marketing in the sales process and the Rev Ops role
summary: Three main lessons on this one: 1. Marketing needs to take responsability of the message and engagement with customers 2. You need to balance the investment in content production & distribution (it is usually tilted more towards the latter) 3. The Rev Ops role is about otimizing pipeline pulling on 4 levers (Data / Process / Enablement / Insights) with insights being a big gap in companies today

name: Reaching the 80% of customers that are not usual gym users
summary: This roundatable tackles ideas & tactics to reach those people that are not regular gym goers. There were 5 main lessons: 1. Understand their concerns and changes in their lifestyle behaviors 2. Adapt your messaging to those concerns 3. Do an assesment of your skills to deliver against their need 4. Complete your offering with partnerships 5. A great experience will drive referrals

name: Become indistrectable
summary:
In this episode, bestselling author Nir Eyal discusses with Chris Hutchins the concept of becoming 'indistractable.' They explore the psychology behind distractions, debunk myths about procrastination, and offer practical strategies to regain focus and productivity. This conversation is crucial for anyone looking to enhance their time management and achieve meaningful progress in their personal and professional lives.

KEY THEMES
• The psychology of distraction — Understanding the hidden psychological triggers that lead to distraction.
• Procrastination misconceptions — Challenging the notion that procrastination is a character flaw.
• Practical strategies for focus — Offering actionable steps to become indistractable and reclaim time.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Distraction is not caused by technology but by internal triggers that need to be managed.
• Insight 2: Procrastination should not be seen as a character flaw but as a symptom of deeper issues.
• Insight 3: To-do lists can be counterproductive; instead, scheduling tasks is more effective.
• Insight 4: Creating a price pact, like burning a $100 bill if you don't follow through, can enhance commitment.
• Insight 5: Differentiating between reactive and reflective work is essential for an indistractable workplace.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Indistractable — A framework for controlling attention and choosing how to spend time.
• Price pact — A commitment strategy where a financial penalty is set for not completing tasks.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""The most important skill of the future is being indistractable." - Nir Eyal"
""Procrastination is not a character flaw; it's a symptom of discomfort." - Nir Eyal"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement a time-blocking strategy instead of relying on to-do lists.
→ Create a price pact to hold yourself accountable for completing tasks.

name: Context, rejecting the premise and creating the future
summary:
This episode of Lochhead on Marketing discusses the importance of 'thinking about thinking' and how rejecting established premises can lead to innovative strategies. Christopher Lochhead emphasizes the significance of context over content in strategic discussions and challenges listeners to create new markets rather than competing in existing ones.

KEY THEMES
• The importance of context in strategic thinking
• The power of rejecting established premises
• Creating new markets rather than competing in existing ones

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Context matters more than content in strategy discussions.
• Insight 2: A strong bias to action can lead to insufficient consideration of context.
• Insight 3: Legendary entrepreneurs and marketers often start by rejecting the premise.
• Insight 4: Rejecting the premise allows for new thinking not tied to past experiences.
• Insight 5: Creating your own market can be more advantageous than competing in existing ones.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Rejecting the premise: A strategy to foster new thinking and innovation.
• Creating your own market: A concept that suggests designing a unique market space to avoid competition.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""A strong bias to action means that sometimes, and I know I’ve been guilty of this more times than I will ever know, we spring to action without doing enough thinking." – Christopher Lochhead"
""Legendary category designers, legendary entrepreneurs, creators, and marketers reject the premise." – Christopher Lochhead"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider the context thoroughly before taking action in strategic discussions.
→ Challenge existing premises to explore new possibilities and create innovative strategies.

name: Pillars behind Nike´s D2C success
summary: Nike has been able to increase their DTC model to representis a third of their sales, which also increases gross margin. In this insightful episode of After Hourse they cover three pillars behind their success: 1. making it experiential 2. Making it hyper localised 3. Driving memberships

name: Facebook´s approach to sport content
summary: Interesting view on how Facebook approaches building, engaging and monetizing users through fan content as well as opportunities around live sports.

name: Grow yourself, grow your business (The three selves)
summary: "Believe in yourself and act like it." Another awesome quote from another awesome episode of The Tim Ferriss Show with lessons anybody can benefit from: 1. People burn out (you or your team) not because they work too much, but because they have a sense of "wasting time." 2. Consider doing a pre-morten with your founders 3. 360 feedback is a must for any leader 4. Consider the 3 word exercise as a previous step to the 360. This basically consists of asking people to define you in 3 words and match their perceptions with your beliefs. 5. Life is about the obstacles; don´t run away from them 6. The three selves framework: Self awareness, self compassion and self talk. Self talk is  a powerful lever (positive or negative) so try to make it as encouraging as possible.

name: The power of questions to help you grow
summary:
In this episode, Marc Champagne discusses his new book, Personal Socrates, which explores the transformative power of asking the right questions. By drawing on insights from renowned figures like Kobe Bryant, Maya Angelou, and Steven Hawking, Marc illustrates how pivotal questions can lead to significant personal growth and change.

KEY THEMES
• The transformative power of questions — How asking the right questions can lead to personal growth.
• Insights from world-class performers — Learning from the experiences and questions of successful individuals.
• Personal development through introspection — Using introspective questions to change one's life trajectory.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Questions can be a catalyst for personal transformation.
• Insight 2: Learning from the questions posed by successful figures can provide guidance in one's own life.
• Insight 3: Introspection and self-questioning are crucial for personal development.
• Insight 4: The right question can lead to a different perspective or life path.
• Insight 5: Marc Champagne's book, Personal Socrates, compiles powerful questions from influential figures.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Personal Socrates — A book by Marc Champagne that uses questions from famous figures to inspire personal growth.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"We're all just one question away from a different life."
"Using strong questions from legends and world-class performers like Kobe Bryant, Maya Angelou, and Steven Hawking."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Reflect on personal challenges by asking transformative questions inspired by successful figures.
→ Read Personal Socrates to explore how questions can lead to personal growth.

name: What content marketers can learn from journalists
summary: Content Marketing usually relies on storytelling to break the attention barrier. In this sense, this episode of the Actionable Marketing Podcast shares 3 main traits that marketers can learn from journalists, which are "master storytellers:" 1. Humans are wired to "engage" with stories 2. Adapt to the reader´s intent 3. Research & depth give credibility and so does framing the story from the perspective of an actual user that wen through the same thought process as your potential customer.

name: Your content wins in distribution & repurposing
summary: Insightful episode on Marketing Spark with 3 main lessons to help your content marketing efforts: 1. You need to establish user / channel / content fit 2. Repurposing is a powerful level to expand reach 3. Understand your audience & develop content for "humans" and then optimize for "robots." Then, they also discuss a few trends to look into such as communities or Tik Tok.

name: Allyson Felix on overcoming challenges and overcoming defeat
summary: Interview where she shares challenges, anecdotes, and her relationship with Nike

name: Understanding Facebook´s quest for the metaverse

name: Driving content creation through AI with WSC Sports
summary: Explanation of the origins, opportunities & features that WSC sports offers to customers. They work with major sport properties to offer their fans personalized content.

name: La especialización es para los mosquitos: Los humanos debemos ser generalistas
summary:
This episode explores the idea that humans should be generalists rather than specialists, drawing from the speaker's experiences and reflections on lifelong learning. It ties together various themes discussed in previous podcast episodes, offering a cohesive narrative on personal and professional growth.

KEY THEMES
• Generalism vs. Specialization — The episode argues for the value of being a generalist rather than a specialist.
• Lifelong Learning — Emphasizes the importance of continuous learning throughout one's life.
• Impostor Syndrome — Discusses the challenges and personal growth associated with feelings of inadequacy in professional settings.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The speaker frequently finds themselves in situations that challenge their impostor syndrome, suggesting that growth often comes from discomfort.
• Insight 2: The episode is a reflection on the speaker's learning journey over nearly three years of podcasting.
• Insight 3: The idea that 'specialization is for insects' suggests that humans benefit from a broad range of skills and knowledge.
• Insight 4: The speaker chose to re-record a talk instead of using the original, indicating a commitment to quality and improvement.
• Insight 5: The episode aims to spark curiosity in listeners, encouraging them to explore topics further.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Generalism — The concept that humans should cultivate a broad range of skills and knowledge rather than specializing in one area.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“La especialización es para los insectos.”"
"“Os preguntaréis qué hago aquí. Yo también me lo pregunto.”"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Reflect on your own learning journey and consider how you can incorporate more generalist skills.
→ Challenge yourself by stepping into situations that may trigger impostor syndrome to foster personal growth.

name: Become & acknowledge a better a you
summary:
In this episode, organizational psychologist Benjamin Hardy discusses the concept of 'The Gap and the Gain,' which he co-authored with Dan Sullivan. The conversation focuses on how high achievers often measure their progress against unreachable ideals, leading to dissatisfaction. Instead, Hardy suggests measuring progress against one's past self to build confidence and happiness.

KEY THEMES
• The Gap vs. The Gain — Measuring progress against ideals versus past achievements.
• Self-Determined Motivation — Focusing on intrinsic desires rather than external validation.
• Reframing Experiences — Turning challenges into gains by focusing on learning and growth.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: High achievers often feel unsatisfied because they measure progress against ever-moving ideals.
• Insight 2: Measuring progress against past achievements (the gain) builds confidence and happiness.
• Insight 3: Social media and societal norms often push people into 'the gap' by promoting external reference points.
• Insight 4: True motivation comes from wanting something for its own sake, not from needing to justify it.
• Insight 5: Being in 'the gain' allows individuals to appreciate their current state and progress, rather than constantly chasing future goals.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• The Gap and the Gain — A concept that encourages measuring progress against past achievements rather than ideals.
• Self-Determination Theory — A psychological framework that emphasizes intrinsic motivation and personal growth.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Ernest Hemingway: 'There's nothing noble about being superior to other people; true nobility is about being superior to your former self.'"
"Benjamin Hardy: 'You don't see the world as it is, you see it as you are.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Practice measuring your progress against your past self regularly to build confidence.
→ Reframe challenges as opportunities for growth and learning to stay in 'the gain.'

name: A masterclass on organic content
summary: Kathleen Booth shares publishes a masterclass on creating organic content. They touch upon a process that includes understanding the phase of the funnel your audience is in, the search intent (who and why), technical aspects to remember, the value of focusing on fewer platforms publishing frequency or how top of the funnel content works best with paid media support while lower funnel is best with word of mouth or organic

name: Masterclass on growth, differentiation , good marketers, and coherent customer journeys
summary: A few golden nuggets from a man who has advised some of the most successful B2B brands. The main lessons include: 1. Look for marketers that have succeeded with average products (vs awesome products) 2. Your business needs to create new or improved "must haves," don´t compete on features 3. It does not always make sense to "create category." 4. To win you need be better and differentiated 5. Choose the customers you can serve best and those that are most profitable and that refer you most. 6. You need to focus on competition, the reality is that customers are comparing so it does not make sense to solely talk about yourself 7. Differentiation is about standing out vs the competition. Providing  a clear reason to believe that is unique 8. You need coherence across the entire journey (from acquisition to purchase); it does not make sense to personalize landings for leads but then have the same conversion path. You need to segment the funnel. 9. You need to go out proactively for customers; do not rely on the "landing + lead generation" tactic

name: Heavy podcast listeners, 5g
summary:
This episode explores new forecasts from Insider Intelligence, focusing on global trends in podcast listenership, 5G adoption, and connected car technology. The discussion also delves into the advertising potential among heavy podcast listeners, the increasing prevalence of paywalls, and the potential for audio glasses to become mainstream. Insights are provided by senior forecasting analysts Peter Vahle and Peter Newman.

KEY THEMES
• Podcast Listenership Trends — Examination of global podcast listener forecasts and their implications.
• 5G Adoption — Insights into the growth of 5G users worldwide.
• Connected Car Technology — Discussion on the rise of connected car drivers and its impact.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Heavy podcast listeners show a high receptiveness to advertisements, presenting a valuable opportunity for marketers.
• Insight 2: The rise of paywalls is reshaping the media landscape, influencing how content is accessed and monetized.
• Insight 3: Audio glasses are being explored as a potential mass-market product, though their future remains uncertain.
• Insight 4: The global adoption of 5G technology is accelerating, with significant implications for connectivity and mobile experiences.
• Insight 5: Connected car technology is gaining traction, offering new opportunities for innovation in the automotive industry.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Forecasting — The process of predicting future trends based on current data, as applied to podcast listeners, 5G users, and connected car drivers.
• Paywalls — A monetization strategy where access to content is restricted to paying subscribers.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Heavy podcast listeners are particularly receptive to ads, making them a prime target for marketers."
"The rise of paywalls is changing how we access and value content in the digital age."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Marketers should consider targeting heavy podcast listeners due to their high receptiveness to advertisements.
→ Businesses should explore the potential of audio glasses as an emerging market opportunity.

name: The origins of Title Nine: Women´s Sport Apparel
summary:
This episode explores the founding of Title Nine, a women's sports apparel company, by Missy Park. Inspired by the opportunities created by Title IX, Missy launched the company in 1989 to fill the gap in the market for women's activewear. The episode highlights her journey from a mail-order catalog to a $100 million business, all without external investment.

KEY THEMES
• Entrepreneurship in Women's Sports Apparel — Missy Park's journey to create a brand for women athletes.
• Impact of Title IX — How the 1972 law influenced opportunities for women in sports and inspired the company's name.
• Growth Without External Investment — Title Nine's success as a self-funded business.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Missy Park founded Title Nine in 1989 to address the lack of suitable activewear for women.
• Insight 2: The company was named after Title IX, reflecting its mission to support women in sports.
• Insight 3: Title Nine started as a mail-order catalog featuring running shorts, tights, and sports bras.
• Insight 4: The business grew to a $100 million company without taking outside investment.
• Insight 5: Missy Park remains the sole owner of Title Nine, highlighting a unique business model.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Title IX — A 1972 law that prohibits sex-based discrimination in federally funded education programs, which opened doors for women in sports.
• Bootstrapping — Building a company without external investment, as demonstrated by Title Nine's growth strategy.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Missy Park: 'We kept hitting singles.'"
"Missy Park: 'Title Nine opened doors for me to compete.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider the potential of niche markets that are underserved, as Missy Park did with women's activewear.
→ Explore bootstrapping as a viable strategy for growing a business without external investment.

name: More details on the tensión between Fifa & EA Sports
summary: It explains both sides and what they hope to get out of the deal in the future. FIFA wants 300 million each year (vs current 150 m) and limit rights to EA to develop new venues for growth such as highlights, NFTs, etc.

name: EA Sports: The current sources of revenue, future opportunities, customer segments & FIFA
summary: Great to understand the current business, future opportunities and the tension between EA & FIFA. Currently, EA gets revenue from the sales of the game, features bought during fantasy and live content (Ultimate) and sponsorship (the snallest). In the future, the believe that "access" will be the key business model driver.

name: More on understanding Pinterest and how to use it for your business
summary: In the past we have already shared that if you have not done so already, Pinterest is one of the most interest channels that your sport or fitness business could explore. In this episode of The Search Engine Journal Podcast, they go into details on features and tactics you could start testing to acquire more customers. The organic possibilities are quite interesting, the development of new advertising features, and the fact that "inspirational," "fitness" and "fashion " content works great in there definitely makes it worth considering...

name: McKinsey on turning customers into fans
summary: McKinsey shares 8 levers business can pull to convert customers into fans. In essence, the goal is to enable engagement, segmentation and ultimately, personalization. Customers are more "convenience-focused" than "brand loyalist" so it helps to try new ways to keep winning customers over

name: Digital vs Analog Businesses
summary:
This episode explores the balance between digital and analog systems in modern businesses, featuring insights from Robert Siegel, a venture capitalist and Stanford lecturer. Siegel discusses his book, 'The Brains and Brawn Company,' which examines the necessity of blending digital innovation with physical operations to create successful companies in an increasingly interconnected world.

KEY THEMES
• Digital Transformation — The necessity and limitations of digital transformation in business.
• Brains and Brawn — The importance of balancing creative, analytical, and physical aspects in a company.
• Hybrid Business Models — The need for a mix of digital and analog systems tailored to each business.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Digital transformation is necessary but not sufficient for business success.
• Insight 2: Companies need a blend of digital (brains) and physical (brawn) components to thrive.
• Insight 3: Purely digital business models are not sustainable in a world that requires integration of physical elements.
• Insight 4: The optimal digital-analog mix varies by company, depending on their specific systems and needs.
• Insight 5: Even digital processes require analog competencies, such as logistics and customer experience.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• The Brains and Brawn Company — A framework for understanding the balance between digital and physical business components.
• Digital Transformation — A concept describing the integration of digital technology into all areas of a business.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Digital transformation is kind of necessary, but not sufficient." – Robert Siegel"
""Those companies aren’t going to be successful as we get into a world where things are increasingly blended between digital and physical." – Robert Siegel"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate your business systems to determine where digital improvements can enhance efficiency.
→ Consider the necessary analog components that support digital operations, such as logistics and customer service.

name: A guide to the elimination of 3rd party cookies
summary: This is a great resource to understand the concept of the 3rd party cookie, why it is going away and what brands can do about it going forward.

name: Your marketing relies on zero-party data & owned marketing
summary:
This episode discusses the importance of zero-party data and owned marketing in the wake of rising ad costs and consumer privacy changes. It highlights how brands can leverage zero-party data to create personalized marketing strategies that build trust and engagement with customers, moving away from reliance on third-party data.

KEY THEMES
• Zero-party data — Importance of collecting data that customers willingly share to personalize marketing.
• Owned marketing — Utilizing brand-controlled channels like email and SMS for effective engagement.
• Consumer privacy changes — Impact of iOS updates and the decline of third-party cookies on marketing strategies.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Zero-party data is preferred by customers as it is shared intentionally and willingly, making it less intrusive.
• Insight 2: Owned marketing involves using channels like email, SMS, and websites that brands fully control.
• Insight 3: Personalization is crucial, with 63% of consumers stopping purchases due to poor personalization.
• Insight 4: Zero-party data allows for highly personalized marketing campaigns, increasing engagement and conversion rates.
• Insight 5: Interactive tools like quizzes and pop-ups can effectively collect zero-party data and enhance customer segmentation.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Zero-party data — Data shared intentionally by customers, including preferences and demographics.
• Owned marketing — Strategy using brand-controlled channels for direct customer engagement.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“It’s time for marketing as usual to change.” - Klaviyo"
"“With zero-party data, brands are significantly diminishing their dependence on third-party advertisers and building meaningful relationships based on personalization and trust.” - Matt Schlicht"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement interactive pop-ups or quizzes to collect zero-party data from customers.
→ Focus on personalizing communication through owned channels to enhance customer engagement.

name: How Apple´s MPP affects email marketing
summary:
This episode discusses the impact of Apple's Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) update on email marketing. It explores how the update affects open rate metrics and suggests strategies for marketers to adapt to these changes, emphasizing the importance of focusing on more meaningful engagement metrics.

KEY THEMES
• Impact of Apple's MPP on email marketing — Apple's update changes how open rates are tracked, affecting marketers' ability to measure engagement.
• Adapting to new metrics — Marketers need to shift focus from open rates to more reliable metrics like click-through rates and conversions.
• Resilience and evolution of email marketing — Despite changes, email marketing remains a powerful tool, requiring adaptation and innovation.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Apple's MPP update hides IP addresses and prevents accurate tracking of email opens, skewing open rate data.
• Insight 2: Open rates are becoming unreliable, prompting a shift towards metrics like click-through rates and conversions.
• Insight 3: MPP adoption is expected to be high, with significant impacts on email marketing practices and metrics.
• Insight 4: Marketers need to adapt workflows and strategies, focusing on deeper engagement and personalization.
• Insight 5: The evolution of email marketing metrics could lead to more comprehensive reporting, integrating multiple data points.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Mail Privacy Protection (MPP) — Apple's update that impacts email open tracking by hiding IP addresses and loading content through a proxy.
• Downstream metrics — Metrics like click-through rates and conversions that provide a more accurate measure of email marketing success.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Open rates have always been a borderline vanity metric."
"MPP might just be the evolutionary tipping point that breaks email marketing out of its silo."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Shift focus from open rates to click-through rates and conversions for measuring email marketing success.
→ Segment email lists to exclude Apple users for more accurate open rate data.

name: Building & growing Hubspot
summary: Interview to the founder. Amazing his take on climate change and the lessons from the Grateful Dead on marketing

name: Pinterest tactics for B2B
summary: Explains the concept of "idea pins" and how B2B business can leverage them

name: Modeling your marketing vs the product lifecycle
summary:
Each stage of the product lifecycle will dictate how you market your product and where you position your brand in the marketplace.
Here’s a recap of the key takeaways from each phase:
Development: Begin building brand awareness ahead of launch to attract early adopters.
Introduction: Let marketing be led by your pricing and promotion strategy. If your product is priced high, focus on educating your audience on the benefits. If you want to reach a lot of people quickly, focus on social proof and influencer marketing.
Growth: Use audience and competitor research to establish brand presence by creating content that your target market wants.
Maturity: If your product is continually improved, build campaigns around new features and benefits. If not, brand equity is your strongest asset.
Decline: Prolong decline by using social proof and brand advocates to attract late adopters.

name: Full guide to Understand CAC & LTV
summary: We are firm believers that LTV & CAC are, in most cases, the metrics that matter for any business, which is why we believe this guide by CXL is awesome. It provides great level of detail on calculating both metrics, why the matter, examples, etc.

name: Attracting high value customers with no advertising
summary: This episode The Predictable Revenue podcast was full of nuggets. It tackles methods to drive high value customers without having to pay for advertising. Some of the main ideas include: The concept of the "brown box" in terms of waiting for customers to "discover" you, you should be a colorful box that stands out from the outside, becoming an authority on a topic vs being an expert, matching the message and language between what your audience wants and what you offer (focusing on the outcomes that you deliver, not on what you do), the levels of influence (imposed influence, collaborative influence, etc.), focusing on the value you will deliver to the customer, during a solution build a collaborative conversation and why they need to solve the problem (even if they do not pick you), The DNQC formula (Data or Info, Narrative, Quantify the investment, Confirm ). People make 3 investments when they hire you (emotional investment, time investment, money investment)

name: The road to Net Zero for Formula E, Bundesliga and others
summary:
This episode discusses the path to achieving net zero carbon emissions within the sports industry, focusing on the efforts of Formula E, VfL Wolfsburg, and the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games. It highlights the importance of concrete emissions reduction strategies and partnerships to meet the goals of the Paris Climate Agreement and the UNFCCC Sports for Climate Action Framework.

KEY THEMES
• Net Zero in Sports — The importance of sports organizations committing to net zero emissions and the challenges involved.
• Emissions Reduction Strategies — Concrete steps and strategies sports organizations are taking to reduce their carbon footprint.
• Role of Partnerships — The critical role of partnerships with suppliers and other stakeholders in achieving sustainability goals.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Formula E has reduced its carbon footprint significantly and is working with DHL on a sustainable freight roadmap.
• Insight 2: The Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games aims to be the most sustainable in history, offsetting emissions through a reforestation project.
• Insight 3: VfL Wolfsburg is targeting a 55% reduction in emissions by 2030, focusing on fan travel as a major source of emissions.
• Insight 4: Formula 1 is developing sustainable fuels, aiming for 100% renewable fuel by the mid-2020s.
• Insight 5: SailGP is reducing freight emissions and has partnered with the Carbon Disclosure Project to encourage environmental data disclosure.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• UNFCCC Sports for Climate Action Framework — A mechanism to reduce the sports industry's carbon footprint.
• Science-based targets — Emission reduction targets aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5℃ above pre-industrial levels.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Patricia Espinosa: 'The sports industry can achieve this before then – I’m absolutely confident.'"
"Julia Pallé: 'We have been working with them on a sustainable freight roadmap, which has been an integral part of our science-based targets submission.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Sports organizations should commit to the UNFCCC Sports for Climate Action Framework to align with global climate goals.
→ Organizations should engage with suppliers to incorporate social and environmental commitments into procurement processes.

name: Current Facebook Marketing Trends
summary: The Not For Lazy Marketers Podcast shares practical tips to leverage from the current Facebook marketing trends including testing content to mitigate the algorithm changes, dynamic advertising, short form videos and visibility ads as a way to generate traffic to your brands.

name: Getting started with Pinterest Ads
summary: A brief introduction to Pinterest Ads, which is usually neglected as a channel to drive traffic (wrongly so). It works better with B2C models although some B2B could work; it is a site where people o to find ideas and have a certain degree of intent. The process includes, objective, targetting and creative.

name: Languising: What it is & how to fight it
summary: This episode is fantastic, feels true in many levels. Languising is a feeling of stagnation, apathy, emptiness, etc. To fight it, you need to enter a state of flow, which has 3 levers: Mastery, Mindfulness (focus) & Mattery. Usually, flow is at it best when you enter it with people you flow (Mario kart example)

name: Changes that could impact your audience projected reach
summary: Facebook is also making a few changes to their advertising product. From now on, it will treat user Facebook & Instagram accounts as separate individuals (unless they purposely link them...). This can impact your projected audience when creating advertising campaigns, so make sure you understand what happens behind the numbers...

name: Happiness: A lever to grow yourself, your people and even, your business
summary:
We live in an era where people are struggling to find a new meaning to the word Happiness. In this remarkable episode of Guy Kawasaki´s podcast they deep dive into the topic from many angles. In essence, happiness has traditionally had three levels (being true to yourself, enjoying daily pleasures and working towards something greater than ourselves), but today we are defining a fourth degree of happiness that is yet to be defined. We also need to remember that happiness is not a "steady" state, there are highs and lows we need to appreciate.
Finally, the episode also focuses on happiness as an asset for any company and gives tactical advice for any leader looking to raise its levels among peers and the entire organization.

name: Why presentations suck & how to fix them
summary:
This episode of Lochhead on Marketing features Dushka Zapata and Dan Roam discussing the elements of effective presentations and why many fail. They explore how simplifying communication and using visual aids can significantly enhance the clarity and impact of presentations, making them more memorable and effective.

KEY THEMES
• The Importance of Simplicity — Simplifying complex ideas into clear, concise messages is crucial for effective communication.
• Visual Communication — Using drawings and visual aids can help convey ideas more clearly and engage audiences.
• Personal Branding — Articulating who you are and what you do is essential for both individuals and companies in developing a strong brand.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Many presentations fail because they are overly complex and not clear.
• Insight 2: Visual aids, like sketches on napkins, can help clarify and communicate ideas effectively.
• Insight 3: People who think differently are increasingly valued in today's world.
• Insight 4: Articulating a clear identity and message is crucial for personal and corporate branding.
• Insight 5: Drawing can transform a meeting's dynamics, moving it from combative to collaborative.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• The Back of the Napkin — A concept that emphasizes using simple sketches to solve problems and communicate ideas effectively.
• Business Doodling — The practice of using drawings to clarify and communicate complex business concepts.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Some of the very, very best ideas come from a simple sketch, invariably drawn on a bar somewhere between a couple of people who are sitting there talking about their idea. - Dan Roam"
"My teacher said that I drew too much, and I talked too much. What that teacher didn’t realize is that I was really struggling to learn to read. - Dan Roam"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Simplify your presentation content to make it more accessible and impactful.
→ Incorporate visual elements like sketches to enhance understanding and engagement during presentations.

name: Embracing Augmented Reality (AR) to create awareness for your brand
summary: Sport brands need to consider embracing new technologies within the core of their business to help them achieve their strategic objectives. This is the topic of this interesting Brandingmag article in which they covered ways to acquire new customers using Augmented Reality.

name: eMarketer Trends Report: Digital Fitness to drive the convergence of content & commerce
summary:
This episode discusses the convergence of content and commerce in 2021, with a focus on digital fitness as a key trend. It highlights the role of major brands like Peloton and Apple in driving this trend, the impact of the pandemic on consumer behavior, and the growing adoption of digital services by baby boomers. These developments offer new opportunities and challenges for marketers.

KEY THEMES
• Convergence of content and commerce — Digital fitness is merging with commerce, led by aspirational brands.
• Pandemic acceleration — The pandemic has accelerated the adoption of digital fitness and related technologies.
• Boomer adoption of technology — Baby boomers are increasingly adopting digital services, influenced by pandemic experiences.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Digital fitness is emerging as a major trend, driven by sophisticated wearables and personalized health tracking.
• Insight 2: The pandemic has accelerated the shift from in-person fitness venues to digital platforms.
• Insight 3: Food delivery apps have seen significant growth, doubling sales from 2019 to 2020.
• Insight 4: Baby boomers are beginning to adopt more recent technologies, partly due to positive telemedicine experiences.
• Insight 5: Marketers may need to adjust their strategies to engage with consumers through digital fitness, telemedicine, and food delivery services.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Digital fitness — A megatrend involving wearables, health tracking, and digital media experiences.
• Convergence of content and commerce — The blending of digital content with commercial opportunities.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Digital fitness is an emerging megatrend, and not just because of the pandemic," said Andrew Lipsman, eMarketer principal analyst at Insider Intelligence."
""The pandemic simply accelerated these trends as consumers adapted to fitness experiences without gyms as the focal point.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Marketers should explore new ways to engage with consumers through digital fitness platforms.
→ Consider targeting baby boomers with digital services, as they are increasingly adopting new technologies.

name: Andy Crestodina and "Where to Start in Digital Marketing?"
summary:
In this episode, Andy Crestodina discusses the foundational steps in digital marketing, emphasizing the importance of starting at the end of the lead generation process. By focusing on conversion pages and calls to action, businesses can ensure that their marketing efforts are effective and that they are not losing potential leads due to weak links in the customer journey. This approach is crucial for maximizing the value of all subsequent marketing activities.

KEY THEMES
• Prioritizing Conversion Optimization — Begin with the end of the funnel to ensure all traffic is valuable.
• Reverse Funnel Strategy — Improve each step of the customer journey by working backward from conversion.
• Content Strategy Alignment — Align content marketing efforts with sales processes for maximum impact.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Start by optimizing conversion pages and calls to action to prevent losing leads.
• Insight 2: Use a reverse funnel approach to improve each step of the customer journey.
• Insight 3: Ensure contact pages are functional and informative to capture potential leads.
• Insight 4: Create content that supports the sales process before focusing on attracting new visitors.
• Insight 5: Original research is a powerful content format that can establish authority and attract links.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Reverse Funnel Strategy — A method of improving the customer journey by starting at the end and working backward.
• Zero-Waste Marketing — Creating content that directly supports sales and is shared with prospects.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“If the marketing team isn’t generating leads and providing content to help the sales team close those leads then it’s not doing its job.”"
"“No amount of water can fill a bucket with holes in the bottom.”"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Improve the functionality and content of your contact page to ensure it captures leads effectively.
→ Create sales enablement content that can be used directly in the sales process to support prospects.

name: Debate on "Gated vs Non Gated Content"
summary: Interesting debate on gated vs non gated content. The non gated content side is more aligned to the ideas on the dark web, splitting the funnel, not relying so much on attribution & MQLs, etc. Also, they discuss the best channels to generate demand, which includes a combination of Search, LinkedIn, Facebook, Podcast & Paid ads

name: Messaging masterclass from Canva
summary:
Messaging can be a truly help you differentiate vs the competition and establish a unique position in the market. Canva is an awesome example of a brand that has done so beautifully and in this episode of The Product Marketing Experts podcast they interview their Head of PMM and breakdown their framework in 3 steps:
•	Identifying audience insights which in essence, is researching your customers or potential customers to determine the need they have
•	Crafting your message, which should look to define the "jobs to be done," key language to use to establish that unique position, the "reason to believe," etc.
•	Testing & iterating to validate that the messaging really resonates with your audience.
•	Check with internal stakeholders and drive employee enablement so that the entire organizations embraces the messaging playbook to ensure a unified language across the different touchpoints and phases of the funnels

name: Marketing lessons from Panasonic
summary: Japanese brands obsess about the customer. In that sense, their framework relies on 3 guiding principles: 1. Being agile 2. Being relevant 3. Being fearless (This includes asking people in performance reviews how many new things they tried). When looking at others to learn, look to understand WHY things work (the context), not just the what.

name: Understanding the future of NFTs
summary: Review of what NFTs, current & future opportunities and even a sport based business model.

name: Conversión en Mobile
summary: Conversion today is mostly won in mobile. Main findings: 1. Font size at least 16 pixels 2. CTA need to stand out 3. Integration with other platform to improve UX 4. Simplicity 5. Watch out for Cookie Banners 6. Sticky that it is not mixed with cell phone

name: The tough road towards Olympic Gold
summary:
This episode features a conversation with professional volleyball players and Olympians Alix Klineman and April Ross, known as The A-Team. They discuss their journey to winning the gold medal at the 2020 Summer Olympics, the formation of their partnership, and the mental and emotional challenges they faced along the way. The episode highlights the importance of trust, perseverance, and following one's passion in achieving success.

KEY THEMES
• The power of partnership — Alix and April's collaboration and mutual respect were crucial to their success.
• Overcoming adversity — Both athletes faced personal and professional challenges, which they navigated through self-reflection and determination.
• Mental resilience — The importance of mental fortitude and strategies to manage anxiety and pressure in high-stakes environments.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Alix and April's undefeated run at the Olympics was a result of their consistent practice and high standards.
• Insight 2: April's decision to continue her career post-Rio was driven by a deep, intrinsic motivation to achieve her goals.
• Insight 3: Alix transitioned to beach volleyball with conviction, despite initial setbacks and financial uncertainty.
• Insight 4: Both athletes emphasize the importance of being true to oneself and not being overly concerned with others' perceptions.
• Insight 5: They highlight the significance of consistent work and trust in oneself to achieve high performance levels.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Practice winning — The concept of putting pressure on oneself during practice to simulate high-stakes competition.
• Growth mindset — Alix's approach to learning and improving by being open-minded and realistic about her starting point.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"April: 'Win in practice. Practice winning.'"
"Alix: 'Figure out what you want and don’t let anybody tell you no.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Listeners should focus on consistent practice and maintaining high standards to improve performance.
→ Follow your heart and pursue what feels authentic, filtering advice through a personal lens.

name: Why a "Content Gap Analysis" can help you improve conversions
summary:
Prior to making a purchase decision, customers seek for content that will help them solve doubts, learn greater details about a product or service, etc. In that sense, you probably know that not all of your customers are in the same phase of the sales funnel (or customer journey). As such, you need to make sure that the content you put out is relevant to each customer and the stage they are in within the purchasing process.
The problem comes when you are missing out on topics that could be of great significance for your target audience. This is usually done through a "Content Analysis Gap" and this article from SEO Journal may be of great help. They cover a 4 step processes to carry out such analysis successfully which includes:
Mapping out the Buyer´s Journey
Conduct Market Research
Analyze the content of your web
Monitor the competition
You might pick up a few new ideas which can be of value for your sport or fitness organization.

name: Testing ads on Facebook Messenger
summary:
This episode explores the strategic use of Facebook Messenger Ads, detailing their two main types: 'click-to-message' and 'sponsored message'. It highlights the benefits of these ads in fostering direct conversations with users, which can enhance relationship-building and increase conversions.

KEY THEMES
• Facebook Messenger Ads — Understanding the two types and their purposes.
• Direct User Engagement — Leveraging Messenger Ads to foster conversations and build relationships.
• Ad Optimization — Strategies for setting up and optimizing Messenger Ads for better engagement.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Facebook Messenger Ads can be categorized into 'click-to-message' and 'sponsored message', each serving distinct purposes.
• Insight 2: 'Click-to-message' ads aim to initiate private conversations with users, enhancing customer interaction and lead nurturing.
• Insight 3: 'Sponsored message' ads appear in users' Messenger inboxes, prompting them to engage directly with the brand.
• Insight 4: Messenger Ads stand out by bypassing the crowded newsfeed, capturing user attention more effectively.
• Insight 5: Using Messenger Ads can differentiate brands by providing unique interaction opportunities, crucial for relationship-building.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Click-to-message Ads — Designed to prompt users to send a private message, facilitating direct engagement.
• Sponsored Message Ads — Ads that appear in Messenger inboxes, encouraging users to interact as if they received a message from a contact.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Opening the door for conversation can be an incredibly powerful selling tool."
"In a time when the newsfeed is busier than ever, any small advantage you have in standing out—or skipping the newsfeed altogether—is worth taking."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Consider using Facebook Messenger Ads to initiate direct conversations with potential leads.
→ Utilize social media management tools like Hootsuite to manage and respond to incoming messages efficiently.

name: Power your video lead generation game
summary:
This episode delves into the evolving landscape of content marketing in the era of AI, highlighting the importance of content governance and authenticity. It discusses how AI engines act as gatekeepers and the impact of AI on content marketing roles, emphasizing strategies for maintaining brand identity and trust in a zero-click environment.

KEY THEMES
• AI as Gatekeepers — AI engines are now crucial in determining brand visibility and identity.
• Content Governance — Ensuring content authenticity and governance is vital in the zero-click era.
• Evolving Marketing Roles — AI is reshaping traditional content and marketing roles, creating a 'ghost workforce'.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: AI engines are the new gatekeepers to brand identity, necessitating robust content governance.
• Insight 2: The zero-click era demands a focus on content authenticity to maintain brand integrity.
• Insight 3: AI is reshaping content marketing roles, leading to a 'ghost workforce' phenomenon.
• Insight 4: Overlooked content assets can significantly drive acquisition success.
• Insight 5: Building a content strategy that survives AI search requires focusing on gravity rather than volume.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• The CRISP Framework — A method to prepare content for agentic AI.
• The Trust Lattice Framework — A structure for measuring content marketing trust in the AI age.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"AI engines are the new gatekeepers to your brand."
"Content governance is one of the biggest tools to ensure they reveal the brand identity you’ve created."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement content governance strategies to maintain brand identity in AI-driven environments.
→ Focus on creating authentic content to thrive in the zero-click era.

name: Lead generation with Vimeo
summary:
Are you currently using video as part of your content marketing strategy? If not, you probably should given the huge potential it has to help you attract new customers for your business.
In that regard, Vimeo has just announced a series of partnerships and tools aimed at helping video creators with their lead generation strategy through the platform. In particular, these will include:
New & enhanced integrations with HubSpot, Mailchimp, and Constant Contact.
Additional tools that allow users to add whichever contact forms they choose to their videos and sync them with their email marketing platform.

name: Using Memes in your content marketing game
summary:
This episode explores the use of memes in content marketing, highlighting their potential to enhance brand engagement and awareness on social media. It discusses the benefits and risks associated with meme usage, emphasizing the importance of wit, relevance, and relatability while cautioning against potential pitfalls like offending audiences or appearing inauthentic.

KEY THEMES
• The Power of Memes — Memes can effectively engage audiences and build brand awareness.
• Risks of Meme Usage — Humor is subjective, and memes can backfire if not used carefully.
• Strategic Considerations — Brands must consider audience, authenticity, and appropriateness when using memes.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Memes can be a cost-effective way for brands to connect with their audience.
• Insight 2: Successful memes require wit, relevance, and relatability.
• Insight 3: Brands risk being labeled 'cringey' if they misuse memes or join trends too late.
• Insight 4: Viral memes can pose brand safety risks if they contain dark humor.
• Insight 5: Brands should evaluate audience, authenticity, and appropriateness before using memes.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Cultural Zeitgeist — Memes allow brands to participate in current cultural conversations.
• 'How Do You Do, Fellow Kids?' — A meme mocking brands that awkwardly try to fit in with trends.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"“Memes are a fun way to enter of-the-moment conversations and jump on the bandwagon of the cultural zeitgeist.” - Sarah Aitken"
"“Many brands have tried to piggyback on an internet trend and fallen flat on their faces.” - Don Caldwell"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate the cultural relevance and timing before using a meme in marketing.
→ Ensure that meme content aligns with the brand's voice and values to maintain authenticity.

name: Why do we procrastinate?
summary:
This episode delves into the reasons behind procrastination, challenging the notion that it's merely a time management issue. Experts discuss how procrastination is often an emotional coping strategy rather than a simple act of laziness, and they offer insights into how understanding and managing emotions can help overcome it.

KEY THEMES
• Procrastination as an emotional coping strategy — Procrastination is more about managing emotions than managing time.
• The role of mood management — Avoiding tasks is often about avoiding negative emotions associated with them.
• Social and self-perception — Concerns about how others perceive us and self-criticism can exacerbate procrastination.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Procrastination is often misinterpreted as a time management problem, but it is more accurately an emotional coping strategy.
• Insight 2: Negative emotions like fear, frustration, and anxiety are often at the root of procrastination.
• Insight 3: Celebrating completed tasks can create positive feelings that encourage further productivity.
• Insight 4: Lack of self-compassion and fear of judgment can increase procrastination tendencies.
• Insight 5: Social support can alleviate some of the stress that leads to procrastination.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Procrastinatory cognition — The pattern of ruminating about one's own procrastination.
• Social esteem — The concern about how others perceive one's abilities, which can lead to procrastination.

NOTABLE QUOTES

name: Learn to create awesome landing pages for your marketing campaigns
summary:

This is the reason why we bring you this awesome guide from Harry´s Marketing Examples with tips and examples on how to do so. The guide is divided in two sections:
Above the fold:
1/ Explain the value you provide (title)
2/ Explain how you'll create it (subtitle)
3/ Let the user visualize it (visual)
4/ Make it believable (social proof)
5/ Make taking the next step easy (Call To Action)
Below the fold:
6/ Make the value concrete (features and objections)
7/ Inspire action (social proof)
8/ Tie up loose ends (FAQ)
9/ Repeat your call to action (2nd Call To Action)
10/ Make yourself memorable (Founder's note)
For each one you will find details and examples in the article so make sure to check it out. The main lesson though, as expressed in the article:
Your landing page is your sales pitch. Never forget this. Examine each element and ask:
Would this help me sell if I met the customer in person?
If not, remove it. If you don't know go out and sell to customers in person.

name: The MLS & "brand clarity" in times of chaos
summary:
We also made time to attend a webinar organized by the Johan Cruyff Institute in which David Bruce, senior vice president of brand and integrated marketing at Major League Soccer (MLS), discussed some of the lessons, insights and the importance of brand purpose when facing these challenging times for sport organizations
What have they learned during a challenging 2020? Mr. Bruce listed the following the main things:
Listen and learn: Where is the sport fan in terms of concerns, expectations, etc.?
Read the room: Sport is not a bubble and sport brands need to identify how they can make positive impact during difficult times.
Brand, Brand, Brand: Brand purpose was the guiding light in decision making across all business areas
Innovation and creation while adopting an agile mentality are key for long term recovery of the business.
Everything in “Beta”: Speed needs to be above perfection. Then, sport fans will provide feedback on what works and what does not. Mr. Bruce then shared this interesting quote on this topic:
"Perfection is the enemy of good. If you need to be right before you move, you will never win" (Michael Ryan, CEO of World Health Organization)
Find your lane in culture: What is the role of your sport brand on culture? Can it help drive positive social change?
Ultimately, the goal of any sport organization should be to drive fan engagement. It is of upmost importance to keep connected to them, specially during times in which attendance to stadiums is banned and "touch points" are limited. The sport fan´s consumption funnel has changed and thus, the marketing processes around it to deliver the experience that maintains the emotional bonds between sport brands and fans.
All these lessons can be summarized in “MLS Unites,” which is one of the main actions the organization carried out during the lock down. The idea was to connect with fans through virtual content with a focus on:
Educating on "covid protocols"
Entertaining fans even from home
Adapting big events through eMLS (gaming)
Building new “moments” (people wanted ideas to do stuff at home such as training, skills, diets, recipes, etc.)
Finally, Mr. Bruce shared some details that might help shape the MLS of the future and that reinforce the idea that their is trust in the medium term future of the league:
New clubs will enter the league: Austin FC is the 27th MLS club
New stadiums are being built
The importance of counting with rising stars and established stars (players and coaches) for the value of the league
How the emergence of young players who played in MLS academies (such as Alphonso Davies or Weston McKennie) that end up becoming global stars is critical for awareness of the league at the global level.
Among the group of owners we can find pop culture stars such as David Beckham, Kevin Durant, Will Ferrel, James Harden or Matthew McConaughey.
Brand purpose: Fans will support those brand that strengthen their ties to social causes
Leverage the brand assets & the presence in culture
As you can see, this was an interesting view of where MLS is and where it is going. We will keep you posted with further relevant developments that may ultimately help you understand how the major sport organizations are shaping the industry.

name: 5g and opportunities for sport
summary:
We had the opportunity to attend a virtual session that covered how 5g will transform the business of sport. In particular, Christine Romans (CNN) interviews Steve Hellmuth, EVP of Media Operations & Technology for the NBA about the specific impact of 5g for the NBA. You can access the webinar through this link but if you prefer a summary, the main ideas or ways in which it could be applied we took out from the conversation were the following:
For the moment, the main focus is to take advantage of how 5g can enable, thanks to its low latency, synchronized views of games in real time with people in other locations. Sometimes, current WIFI speed connections are not the same across different cities, regions or countries and you may be chatting with a friend about a particular game but there may be a 10 second difference between what you both are actually witnessing. 5g solves this issue and it would make it seem as if you were watching the game in the same living room.
Gambling: The idea in mind is to have layovers of potential bets synced with video of live games. That way, "real time" betting is taken to a new level.
Augmented Reality (AR), which would enable broadcasters to show real time statistics, players tracking and other data "on top" of the actual image.
Virtual reality (VR) on the other hand is still a work in progress for sport, so it will take longer for it develop to its full potential.
These were the main ideas but if you want to know more about this topic, in addition to the full session we shared above, we actually have published articles on our blog discussing several ways in which 5g could make an impact on sport in the near future or the potential of artificial intelligence can have in the industry. Feel free to check them out!

name: The three levels of intent
summary:
Tier 1 - Declared Intent
A person at a qualified account comes inbound and asks for a demo or to speak to a salesperson. That’s it. That’s what your marketing team needs to be optimizing for through free, well-distributed, ungated content.
Unfortunately, software has a hard time measuring the things that work well to optimize for declared intent—so companies optimize for tier 2 and 3 instead.
Tier 2: Assumed / Anonymous Intent
Stick it in the assumed/anonymous bucket if you’re assuming contacts have intent based on filters, but nobody on the other end has actually told you that.
Think review sites. You like to think if an account is comparing you on a review site, they have a high intent for your product. But the reality is, if a company found you on that review site and is comparing you to competitors, your marketing has failed. You should have convinced them long before they got to G2 that you were the best option. If they show up on a review site it should only be for validation.
Tier 3: Low or no intent
Unfortunately, this is where most marketing strategies live. You force “intent” onto contacts that never declared anything of the sort. Think gated ebook downloads, newsletter signups, Zoominfo cold calls, etc.
And when you force intent:
Conversion rates are low

"CoachUp.com is the leading sports coaching platform with over 20,000 coaches."

→ Consider applying Jordan's framework for evaluating startups, focusing on founder potential and market opportunities.

summary: Masterclass on Go To Marketing from Zendesk. The main ideas: 1. It all starts with understanding your audience and their needs 2. Plan out an integrated marketing strategy 3. updating touchpoints between brand and customer 4. aligning marketing with sales teams and operations 5. Not being afraid of pulling a product launch at the last minute if it is not ready for the customer to really extract the value from it.

name: Walter Isaacson on curiosity & creativity
summary:
In this episode of The Knowledge Project Podcast, Walter Isaacson explores the role of curiosity in driving creativity among history's greatest innovators, such as Steve Jobs, Leonardo da Vinci, and Jennifer Doudna. Isaacson discusses how these figures harnessed their curiosity to shape the world and delves into the implications of gene editing and artificial intelligence for the future.

KEY THEMES
• Curiosity as a Driver of Innovation — How curiosity fuels creativity and innovation among historical figures.
• Intellectual Honesty in Leadership — The importance of being brutally honest in leadership roles.
• Future of Technology — The ongoing debate about artificial intelligence and its potential to think creatively.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Curiosity is a common trait among great innovators like Steve Jobs and Leonardo da Vinci.
• Insight 2: Intellectual honesty is crucial for effective leadership and management.
• Insight 3: The pandemic has led to a dispersion of people to more culturally vibrant locations due to remote work opportunities.
• Insight 4: Nurturing childhood curiosity can lead to greater creativity in adulthood.
• Insight 5: The debate on whether machines can think creatively continues, with figures like Elon Musk and Bill Gates weighing in.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Intellectual Honesty — A leadership approach that emphasizes brutal honesty for effective management.
• Curiosity-Driven Innovation — The idea that nurturing curiosity can lead to significant creative and innovative breakthroughs.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Intellectual honesty is something that can push people, make people a great leader."
"We’re all curious as kids, until grownups say, 'Quit asking so many dumb questions.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Nurture your natural curiosity to enhance creativity.
→ Embrace intellectual honesty in leadership and management roles.

name: Behind the growth & evolution of Sports Pro Media
summary:
This episode of the Playbook Podcast features a conversation with Nick Meacham, managing director of SportsPro, discussing the company's growth and evolution over the past two years. The discussion highlights SportsPro's international expansion, digital transition, and pandemic management, providing insights into the sports media industry and the company's strategic direction.

KEY THEMES
• International Expansion — How SportsPro navigated its growth into new markets.
• Digital Transition — The shift towards digital platforms and its implications.
• Pandemic Management — Strategies used to maintain confidence and stability during COVID-19.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: SportsPro has successfully expanded internationally, adapting to new markets.
• Insight 2: The company has increased its focus on digital platforms, aligning with industry trends.
• Insight 3: Managing through the pandemic required strategic adjustments to maintain company confidence.
• Insight 4: SportsPro's operations span across OTT, private equity, and talent sectors.
• Insight 5: The company aims to provide a candid, advertorial-free perspective on industry developments.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Over-the-top (OTT) — A method of delivering media content directly to consumers via the internet.
• Private Equity — Investment funds that directly invest in private companies or engage in buyouts of public companies.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"SportsPro operates across many of the spaces that impact our world: over-the-top (OTT), private equity and talent."
"This episode is an advertorial-free, candid wander exploring what is really going on in our sector."

name: "How to win" on brand
summary: Peep Ladja shares, in our view, 3 important ideas to "win:" 1. You cannot compete on functional benefits, you need to win on brand. At the end of the day, you cannot look at competitors. Analyze your customers, their needs and then, make sure your brand is percevied better 2. The goal of having a consulting service around a product is to get them to understand and gain value from the product earlier.  3. Start small, with a niche audience and expand into the mass market over the long term. A personal brand will take 10-15 years to build...

He and Steve talk about the best way to play it and how it shows up in real world situations, from war zones to Steve’s own life.
