• Insight 5: Act with integrity as if you owned the company, rather than focusing on optics.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Cognitive Biases — Biases explain past decisions but don't prevent future mistakes.
• Reflection — A process of learning from experiences by distilling them into actionable insights.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Never make important decisions when you’re tired, emotional, distracted, or in a rush."
"They don’t have twenty years of experience—they have one year of experience repeated twenty times."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Keep a learning journal and reflect every day to learn from experiences.
→ Seek out information from primary sources to ensure accuracy and depth of understanding.

name: The psychology book that is changing Major League Baseball
summary:
Nobel Prize winner Daniel Kahneman is the author of the best-selling book "Thinking Fast and Slow," which, essentially, describes the way in which the human brain makes decisions based on System 1 (to put it simply, a more impulsive type of decisions) and System 2 (which could be described as more rational).
What is interesting about this New York Times article is the way in which this book has been of great influence to several executives in the way they approach the game from a scouting perspective or even the business. Check it out, as regardless of your sport your in, it could change the way you make certain decisions for your organization.

name: The Role of Content in Creating Demand
summary: Content IS the driver of demand...

name: Why & How to develop a "User Generated Content"
summary:
This episode explores the significance of user-generated content (UGC) in social media marketing, highlighting its impact on consumer purchasing decisions and how brands can effectively leverage it. The discussion covers the distinction between traditional UGC and UGC creators, and provides strategies for incorporating UGC into marketing plans to enhance authenticity and community engagement.

KEY THEMES
• The power of UGC in influencing purchasing decisions — UGC is likened to word-of-mouth recommendations, making it a potent tool for brands.
• Difference between UGC and UGC creators — UGC is organic content from consumers, while UGC creators are paid to produce content that mimics UGC.
• Strategies for effective UGC use — Tips for finding, curating, and sharing UGC to align with brand goals and values.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: 80% of respondents in a 2021 study said UGC highly impacts their purchasing decisions.
• Insight 2: UGC is considered more authentic by consumers, being 2.4 times more likely to be viewed as genuine compared to brand-created content.
• Insight 3: UGC creators do not need a large following and are not required to show their face, unlike traditional influencers.
• Insight 4: Video content is a powerful UGC tool, often performing best in terms of engagement and attention retention.
• Insight 5: Brands like Fenty Beauty use UGC to promote inclusivity and reach a diverse audience, showcasing product tutorials and reviews from a wide range of users.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• UGC vs UGC Creators — UGC is organic content from consumers, while UGC creators are paid to produce content that looks like UGC.
• Later's Collect Feature — A tool for finding and curating UGC through tags, mentions, and hashtags.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""UGC is the social media equivalent of a word-of-mouth recommendation.""
""Consumers are 2.4 times more likely to view user-generated content as authentic compared to content created by a brand.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Use Later's tools to find and schedule UGC, ensuring to credit the original creator.
→ Set clear goals for your UGC strategy, such as showcasing product use or sharing real-life reviews.

name: Me & my chatbot
summary: Are you looking into the possibility of implementing a chatbot for your sport or fitness business? It definitely could make all the sense in the world. In fact, we were once involved in a project to do so for a large fitness operator in the Spanish market.

name: Lessons from AirBnB & their amazing comeback
summary:
While we are aware this is not a "sport" related podcast, there are so many similarities between the performance of the overall travel and tourism industries with sport and / or fitness that we are sure you will find this amazing episode of Masters of Scale as valuable as we did.
In it, they interview Brian Chesky, CEO of AirBnB and he shares many of topics that may touch upon what we have experienced in the world of sport, such as:
•	What 2020 was like for him and the most difficult decision he had to make
•	His approach to leadership during the most difficult times
•	The importance of company culture, brand purpose and the community
•	How Covid has helped him "raise the bar" in terms of the quality he should expect from new propose solutions and services.
•	How the company prepared for the IPO it launched and using the S1 document as a strategic roadmap
In essence, he describes AirBnBs "rise like a phoenix" type year, which we are sure that many sport businesses need inspiration from.

name: Sports as a "door opener" for digital broadcasters?
summary:
Movies and TV shows have enabled the rise of OTT platforms in recent years and the entrance of major digital players such as Facebook or Amazon into the space. There is still though, a big gap for digital broadcasters to overcome traditional broadcasters. The question is if sports can be the key element that drives viewership over to digital platforms from traditional cable operators which is the topic of this interesting debate in the eMarketer Podcast. It seems that digital players are still having a tough time in engaging fans with live content, which is the main reason why people watch sports, as shown in the following graph.
Traditional broadcasters seem to have an edge still in this space as they are able to ensure better experiences for fans. It remains to be seen though, what happens when digital players are able to match the same quality and assuming they are willing to make big investments in the arena...

name: From top gymnast to CMO at Levi´s
summary:
Jim Stengel interviewed Jen Sey, currently CMO at Levi´s, in yet another brilliant masterclass based on brand purpose & vision. It must be noted that Ms. Sey was also a top gymnast during her childhood and we highly enjoyed the leadership lessons she learned during her time as an athlete that she currently applies daily.
If you are looking for an example of someone who transitioned from an elite athlete to developing an amazing business career, then this is an episode you do not want to miss!

name: Storytelling techniques from the world of sports
summary:
This episode explores storytelling techniques from the world of sports, highlighting how these methods can be applied to enhance marketing strategies. It delves into the power of narrative in engaging audiences and building brand loyalty, emphasizing the importance of authenticity and emotional connection in storytelling.

KEY THEMES
• Storytelling in Sports — Examining how sports narratives captivate audiences and create emotional connections.
• Brand Loyalty through Narrative — Using storytelling to build and maintain strong brand loyalty.
• Authenticity in Storytelling — The significance of maintaining authenticity to enhance audience engagement.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Storytelling in sports often involves creating heroes and memorable moments that resonate emotionally with audiences.
• Insight 2: Brands can leverage sports storytelling techniques to create compelling narratives that foster deeper connections with their audience.
• Insight 3: Authenticity in storytelling is crucial for maintaining trust and engagement with the audience.
• Insight 4: Emotional storytelling can significantly enhance brand loyalty by creating a personal connection with the audience.
• Insight 5: The use of real-life stories and testimonials can enhance the authenticity and relatability of brand narratives.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Hero's Journey — A storytelling framework that involves a hero overcoming challenges, often used in sports narratives.
• Emotional Connection — A concept emphasizing the importance of connecting with audiences on an emotional level.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Exact or near-exact quote worth remembering, attributed if possible"
"Another strong quote"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Incorporate storytelling techniques from sports to create engaging brand narratives.
→ Focus on authenticity and emotional connection in your storytelling to build stronger brand loyalty.

name: A guide to "integrated marketing" aimed at helping your business grow.
summary:
Why should you care? Well, in today´s world, in which users have many potential touchpoints with your brand, you want to ensure consistency across all channels in an effort to drive conversions. For example, the content you share on social media must align to your YouTube videos, your web, app, etc.
Only then will you be able to create the necessary brand associations for potential customers to remember your brand that hopefully, drives sales.

name: Branded based SEO vs keyword based
summary:
Not everything in SEO should be "keyword" based. In fact, if you want to drive more conversions and optimize your sales funnel, perhaps you should look into more "branded-based" searches.
Think about it, someone who already knows your brand should me more likely to purchase from you.

name: A view Tokyo 2020 from the commercial perspective
summary: Interesting view of the Olympic games from a commercial partnership perspective

name: Messaging as a key element for brand differentiation
summary:
The folks at CXL share this detailed guide on "messaging" and how it can be a source for brand differentiation and generate demand. The cover the "why" and the "how" through 4 elements that include:
1.	Your USP
2.	Your target
3.	Storytelling
4.	The "messaging guidelines"
They finish it off with a description of how to take it to the market. It has it all!

name: Achieve greater sales figures with these 10 tips
summary:
This episode provides a comprehensive guide to boosting sales productivity through effective onboarding, goal setting, and the use of sales technology. It highlights the importance of intrinsic motivation, continuous training, and strategic prospecting to achieve higher sales figures. The episode is valuable for sales teams aiming to enhance their efficiency and meet sales targets.

KEY THEMES
• Sales Productivity — Enhancing the efficiency of sales teams to meet targets.
• Onboarding and Training — Effective strategies for onboarding new hires and continuous training.
• Sales Technology — Utilizing tools and software to improve sales processes and outcomes.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Companies with effective onboarding processes see a 10% higher sales growth rate.
• Insight 2: High-performing sales teams use nearly 3 times the amount of sales technology as underperforming teams.
• Insight 3: Automating sales processes, such as email sequences, can lead to a 451% increase in qualified leads.
• Insight 4: Intrinsic motivation in salespeople leads to a 46% higher job satisfaction and 16% better performance.
• Insight 5: Time blocking and focusing on high-quality leads can significantly boost sales productivity.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Milestone-based Goals — Setting 30, 60, and 90-day plans for new hires.
• Time Blocking — Dividing the day into blocks dedicated to specific tasks to enhance productivity.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"High-performing sales teams use nearly 3x the amount of sales technology than underperforming teams."
"Salespeople will forget 80-90% of what they learned in training within a month."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement a structured onboarding process with milestone-based goals for new hires.
→ Utilize sales technology tools like CRM, prospecting apps, and communication platforms to enhance productivity.

name: Basics of affiliate marketing to create additional sources of revenue
summary:
If you are looking to generate additional sources of revenues for your small sport or fitness business (or even your personal training practice), and if you have not considered affiliate marketing yet, perhaps it could be a right time to do so.
Why?
Well, if you are a fitness professional for instance, your capacity to influence customers to purchase certain products could be very large. In my case, I work with a personal trainer on a weekly basis and every piece of advice he gives me for me is "the truth." And this applies to the fitness equipment I have purchased to complete my workout routine at home.
Who would provide better advice than you to a customer looking to buy fitness equipment to workout at home a few days? And if that is you, couldn´t you reap some benefits from that knowledge?

name: A "go-to" guide to develop cancellation emails
summary:
In general terms, it is extremely difficult to convince customers of changing their minds once they have decided to stop using your service. This doesn´t mean though that they are "lost and gone" forever. They could return at any point in the future and for that reason it is a good idea to make sure your last interaction with them is a good one, as they will remember this last positive experience if they ever consider your services again.
Thus the reason we thought this detailed guide with best practices and examples of cancellation emails could be useful! It also shares a few ideas on minimizing churn so make sure you pick a few ideas for your business!

name: Lessons on Innovation from Classpass
summary:
This episode features a panel discussion from the 2021 How I Built This Virtual Summit, focusing on innovation with insights from Payal Kadakia of ClassPass, Tristan Walker of Walker and Company, and Perry Chen of Kickstarter. The conversation explores how true innovation stems from authenticity rather than novelty, offering listeners a fresh perspective on creating impactful businesses.

KEY THEMES
• Innovation through Authenticity — Innovation is more about being authentic than introducing something entirely new.
• Entrepreneurial Insights — The panelists share their experiences and insights on building successful companies.
• Impactful Business Strategies — Discussion on strategies that lead to meaningful and lasting business impact.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Innovation does not necessarily mean creating something new; it can be about bringing authenticity to existing ideas.
• Insight 2: Authenticity in business can lead to more sustainable and impactful innovation.
• Insight 3: Successful entrepreneurs often focus on refining and improving existing concepts.
• Insight 4: The panelists emphasize the importance of staying true to one's vision and values.
• Insight 5: Building a business with a focus on authenticity can differentiate it in a crowded market.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Authenticity in Innovation — The idea that staying true to one's values and vision can drive innovation.
• Refinement over Novelty — Focusing on improving existing ideas rather than always seeking to create new ones.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Innovation doesn't require newness, but rather, authenticity."
"Staying true to your vision and values is key to impactful innovation."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Focus on bringing authenticity to your business ideas rather than striving for novelty.
→ Refine and improve existing concepts to create a sustainable business impact.

name: A conversation w/ Bo Han (CEO at Buzzer)
summary:
In this episode, Bo Han, CEO of Buzzer, discusses how his sports media startup is revolutionizing the way fans engage with live sports through real-time notifications and micro-transactions. The conversation explores Buzzer's recent $20 million funding round, its partnerships with major sports leagues, and the evolving preferences of Gen Z sports fans. The episode also touches on the potential realignment in college sports with Texas and Oklahoma considering a move to the SEC.

KEY THEMES
• Innovation in Sports Media — Buzzer's approach to engaging fans with real-time notifications and micro-transactions.
• Generational Shifts — Differences in sports consumption between Gen Z and older fans.
• Strategic Partnerships — Leveraging athlete investors and major league partnerships to grow Buzzer.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Buzzer's platform is designed to capitalize on key moments in sports by sending push notifications to fans.
• Insight 2: The startup has secured $20 million in funding from high-profile athletes, highlighting the importance of strategic investor partnerships.
• Insight 3: Gen Z sports fans prefer athlete-centric content and streaming services over traditional broadcast television.
• Insight 4: Buzzer is currently collaborating with major sports leagues like the NBA, NHL, and PGA Tour, with plans for further expansion.
• Insight 5: There is a potential major shift in college sports with Texas and Oklahoma exploring a move to the SEC.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Micro-transaction Model — Buzzer's use of one-time streaming purchases for specific sports moments.
• Athlete-Centric Distribution — Leveraging athletes as distribution platforms to reach and engage fans.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Bo Han: 'Younger fans are more athlete-centric, more comfortable with streaming as opposed to broadcast television.'"
"Hosts: 'A potential tectonic shift in college sports with Texas and Oklahoma considering joining the SEC.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore partnerships with influential athletes to enhance brand reach and engagement.
→ Consider adopting micro-transaction models to cater to younger, digital-native audiences.

name: When being good is not good enough
summary:
This episode explores the complex nature of defining 'good' in business, using examples like the European Super League and Deliveroo's flotation to illustrate how values and ethics play a crucial role in brand perception and success. The discussion emphasizes the importance of aligning business practices with moral responsibility and the challenges of maintaining a balance between profitability and ethical standards.

KEY THEMES
• The Relativity of 'Good' — Different stakeholders have varying definitions of what constitutes 'good', influenced by their perspectives and interests.
• Ethics in Business — Successful brands must balance profitability with ethical practices and social responsibility.
• Brand Values — Values should guide behavior and differentiate brands, but many fail to implement them effectively.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The European Super League's failure highlights the importance of understanding and aligning with customer values.
• Insight 2: Uber's legal challenges underscore the need for ethical treatment of workers in the gig economy.
• Insight 3: Deliveroo's flotation demonstrated how concerns over worker rights can significantly impact a company's valuation.
• Insight 4: Values should be limited to three — rational, emotional, and aspirational — to be memorable and effective.
• Insight 5: A brand's promise should guide internal behavior and differentiate it from competitors, ensuring long-term relevance.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Brand Values — Three key values (rational, emotional, aspirational) that guide brand behavior and differentiation.
• Brand Promise — A guiding principle that directs internal behavior and motivates differentiation from competitors.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Pep Guardiola: 'Sports is not a sport when the relation between the effort and the success, the effort and the reward doesn’t exist.'"
"Without an ethical stance, businesses and individuals are hollow."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Define and implement three core values (rational, emotional, aspirational) to guide brand behavior.
→ Ensure that brand promises are clear and motivate differentiation while aligning with customer expectations.

name: Facebook ad design guide to increase sales
summary: If you want to take your Facebook advertising game to a new level, you will surely need to focus on improving your creativity. Given the current amount of competition on the platform, you will need to create advertising that literally stops potential customers during their scroll.

name: Execute on your video marketing strategy with these 8 steps
summary:
This episode delves into the transformative power of video email marketing, highlighting its ability to captivate, engage, and convert email subscribers more effectively than traditional text-based emails. By incorporating videos into emails, marketers can create a visually compelling experience that enhances message retention and drives action.

KEY THEMES
• The power of video in email marketing — Videos can engage subscribers more effectively than text, leading to higher retention and conversion rates.
• Creative uses of video in emails — From product demonstrations to personalized greetings, videos offer diverse ways to connect with audiences.
• Implementation strategies — Practical steps and examples for integrating videos into email campaigns to maximize impact.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Videos in emails can lead to a 95% retention rate of the message, significantly higher than text-based emails.
• Insight 2: Thumbnails in emails can indicate video content, prompting viewers to click through to watch.
• Insight 3: Personalized videos can strengthen relationships with subscribers by adding a personal touch.
• Insight 4: Video tutorials and expert interviews can make complex concepts more accessible and engaging.
• Insight 5: Including video testimonials in emails adds credibility and social proof, enhancing persuasion.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Video email marketing — Incorporating videos into emails to enhance engagement and conversion.
• FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) — Using event recap videos to create a sense of urgency and increase future attendance.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Videos provide a visually compelling and immersive experience that can leave a lasting impression."
"Watching a video allows me to see first hand what to do."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Identify opportunities in existing email campaigns where video can enhance messaging and add value.
→ Use a reputable email marketing tool with a drag-and-drop editor to easily incorporate videos into emails.

name: The Right Size Project
summary:
This episode discusses the concept of 'right-sizing' projects, using examples such as Airbus canceling its plane and the shutdown of Quibi. It highlights the importance of aligning project scope with market needs and strategic goals, emphasizing lessons learned from past business ventures.

KEY THEMES
• Project Right-Sizing — Aligning project scope with market demand and strategic objectives.
• Business Failures — Learning from the shutdown of ventures like Quibi.
• Preservation of Knowledge — The importance of maintaining historical business insights.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Airbus's decision to cancel its plane project reflects the necessity of reevaluating project viability.
• Insight 2: Quibi's shutdown highlights the risks of not aligning product offerings with market demand.
• Insight 3: The 'Peanut Butter Memo' suggests spreading resources too thin can lead to inefficiencies.
• Insight 4: Preserving business knowledge over decades can provide valuable insights for future projects.
• Insight 5: Modern portfolio theory can inform strategic decision-making in project management.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Modern Portfolio Theory — A financial framework for maximizing returns while managing risk.
• The Peanut Butter Memo — A metaphor for spreading resources too thin across projects.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"This isn't the full game--you need the game pieces and the booklet to do that."
"Quibi shuts down (only Hollywood noticed)"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate current projects to ensure they are right-sized for market demand.
→ Preserve and review historical business documents to gain insights for future strategies.

name: Seth Godin on "Resilience"
summary:
In this episode, Seth Godin discusses the importance of resilience in a rapidly changing world. He emphasizes that resilience, rather than rigidity, is crucial for thriving when things don't go as planned, offering insights into designing systems and attitudes that adapt to unforeseen circumstances.

KEY THEMES
• Resilience — The ability to adapt and thrive when things don't go as planned.
• Flexibility — Designing systems that are not rigid and can handle unexpected changes.
• Community and Possibility — Leveraging collective strength and an open mindset to navigate challenges.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Resilience is about creating systems that work even when outcomes are unexpected.
• Insight 2: Designing for the best-case scenario is less effective than preparing for when it doesn't happen.
• Insight 3: Fixing on a point on the horizon, like sailors do, helps in navigating through storms.
• Insight 4: Flexibility and community support are critical components of resilience.
• Insight 5: Resilience requires a commitment to a design and attitude that embraces uncertainty.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Resilience — A system and attitude designed to adapt when things don't go as planned.
• Horizon Fixation — A strategy used by sailors to maintain direction during storms.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"The world is going to change, and resilience is our best response."
"Bulletproof is too expensive, too rigid and requires perfect knowledge of the future."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Design systems and strategies that can adapt to unexpected changes.
→ Cultivate flexibility and build community support to enhance resilience.

name: Advertising masterclass with fitness apparel brand "Tala" used as an example
summary:
Charlie Lawrance returns this week with an reviewing Tala´s (a fitness apparel brand) advertising on Facebook. He provides great information such as:
•	The Snap / Benefit / Action copy testing method
•	The importance of including an "core fundamental" offer and a CTA
•	Shooting in different dimensions to enhance creative
•	Why they need to include user reviews or testimonial ads (which we also speak about below...)

name: The 3 levels of intent
summary: These levels are: Low or no Demand / Anonymous or Assumed Demand / High Intent. Then, a Q&A on generating demand across the business

name: Forget about “creating a new category”
summary:
This episode challenges the conventional wisdom of creating a new category in the market. It discusses the pitfalls and inefficiencies of focusing on category creation and suggests alternative strategies for businesses to achieve success. The conversation is relevant for marketers and business leaders looking to optimize their strategies in competitive markets.

KEY THEMES
• The myth of category creation — The episode debunks the idea that creating a new category is essential for business success.
• Alternative strategies — It explores other effective strategies businesses can adopt instead of focusing on category creation.
• Market competition — The discussion highlights how businesses can thrive in competitive markets without creating new categories.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Creating a new category can be resource-intensive and may not always lead to success.
• Insight 2: Businesses can achieve growth by improving existing products or services rather than creating new categories.
• Insight 3: Understanding customer needs and enhancing customer experience can be more beneficial than focusing on category creation.
• Insight 4: Companies should leverage their strengths and existing market presence instead of trying to create a new category.
• Insight 5: Effective marketing and branding can differentiate a business without the need for a new category.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Category creation — The idea that a business can achieve success by creating a new market category.
• Customer-centric strategy — Focusing on understanding and meeting customer needs as a path to success.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Creating a new category is not a guaranteed path to success.""
""Focus on what your customers need rather than trying to invent a new category.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate your business strategy to see if focusing on existing strengths and market presence could be more beneficial than creating a new category.
→ Consider improving customer experience and satisfaction as a way to achieve growth without creating a new category.

name: Going deep into the subscription industry
summary: In it, they review in detail the state of the subscription industry, the type of business who most benefit from a subscription based model, mistakes to avoid or metrics to monitor closely. It has it all! The main idea? That there are three types of suscription businesses: 1. Replenish-based (dollar shave club) 2. Curation (Birchbox) 3. Access to exclusive content

name: 5 ideas to consider when launching limited time offers
summary:
Your sport or fitness business has probably relied on developing some form of offer to try to gain new customers. Sometimes though, we get blinded by the "quick win" possibility in the short term that we forget the impact this has in the future of the brand.
This is the reason why we share this episode from Dan Martell´s Growth Stacking podcast, in which he shares 5 key principles to factor in when designing limited time offers. These include:
•	Understand your "Cost of Goods Sold" (C.O.G.S)
•	Offer more value, not higher price discounts
•	Create bundles
•	Work on your copywriting skills
•	Promote the deal

name: Achieving greatness with Mark Cuban
summary:
Mark Cuban, one of the greatest sport business personalities in the industry, shared some awesome knowledge for sport business owners in yet another fantastic episode of the "Starting Greatness" podcast.
In it, he shares critical lessons he learned at the beginning of his career, regular advice he gives small business owners and the necessary skills to have "the edge," which include having the will to win, focus or having constant competitive awareness.

name: Turning fans into customers in the sport & fitness industries
summary:
Gary Vaynerchuk interviews several top leaders & CMOs from a wide variety of industries centering around one major question: "How can brands turn customers into fans?"
The full episode is full of great insights and real examples but we found it additionally relevant because of two guests included in the line up:
•	Dino Bernacchi, CMO of the NFL´s Cleveland Browns
•	Joey Gonzales, CMO at fitness brand "Barry´s"
Two awesome examples from the world of sport which you can learn from for sure!

name: Get your fitness business in financial shape
summary:
This episode of the podcast provides a comprehensive guide for fitness entrepreneurs on improving their business operations, focusing on membership sales, marketing strategies, and legal considerations. Featuring insights from industry experts like Alan Leach and Jono Petrohilos, the episode covers a range of topics from leveraging Facebook ads to understanding legal agreements tailored for the fitness industry.

KEY THEMES
• Membership Sales — Strategies for attracting and retaining gym members.
• Marketing Strategies — Effective use of social media and data to enhance business growth.
• Legal Considerations — Importance of proper legal agreements to protect fitness businesses.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Alan Leach discusses an ideal membership sales process to attract new members.
• Insight 2: Jono Petrohilos shares best practices for running successful Facebook ads for fitness businesses.
• Insight 3: Conscious Counsel provides a simplified approach to legal agreements tailored for the fitness industry.
• Insight 4: The importance of understanding Customer Acquisition Cost as highlighted by Jamie Owens from Hussle.
• Insight 5: David Minton emphasizes the need for the fitness industry to become data-rich to better handle future crises.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Membership Sales Process — A structured approach to attracting and retaining gym members.
• Customer Acquisition Cost — A metric to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of marketing strategies.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Alan Leach: 'Setting your teams up for continuous success is key to maintaining a thriving membership base.'"
"Jamie Owens: 'Over 50% of gyms surveyed didn't know their Customer Acquisition Cost, which is crucial for strategic planning.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Fitness entrepreneurs should evaluate and optimize their membership sales process to ensure continuous growth.
→ Utilize Facebook ads effectively by targeting the right audience and measuring key metrics to enhance business reach.
publishers: How to Grow Your FItness Business

name: Raise the bar on your Pinterest game
summary:
Alisa Meredith, the host in this insightful episode of the Social Pros Podcast, defines Pinterest as a platform "where people go to plan their best selves."
Now, if you are in the sport or fitness industry, you could play a big part in helping people achieve that, so it makes total sense for you to start pondering a Pinterest strategy if you have not done so already. And if that is not enough, she also shares some amazing data, tools & tactics that will help you raise the bar on your Pinterest and social media game.

name: Resilience in the National Women´s Soccer League
summary:
Guy Raz interviews Lisa Baird, commissioner of the National Women´s Soccer League (United States). 2 days into her job, Ms. Baird had to make the tough decision of closing down the league because of the spread of Covid -19. Since then, she has battled to make a powerful comeback that makes the league even better than it was before. She shares the full details in the episode but let us highlight 3 ideas with you that Ms. Laird mentions:
•	Sometimes, as difficult it may be, you know the what the right decision is and you must act on it decisively.
•	Although it is an extremely challenging time for sport in general, she does identify a realm of opportunity for the league going forward.
•	Her definition of resilience, which basically implies facing a challenge with the resources you have (not caring for the ones other may have) , gather your team around a common cause and set out to "get it done."

name: Reframe your influence marketing game
summary:
Notice though, in the title we took out the "r" from "influencer" marketing to focus specifically on influence marketing. This is the topic of this great episode in the Social Media Examiner podcast, which essentially, describes a framework for you to reframe your influence marketing game.
The goal of influence marketing should be to find someone who is super relevant to your target audience and is capable of driving them to take some form of action with regards to your business. Or put another way, the goal should not be to find an influencer with millions of followers; find those who are able to impact the behavior towards your brand of those you want to do business with.

name: Digital natives don´t want "stuff"
summary:
This episode explores the emergence of 'Native Digitals,' a generation for whom digital life is primary, and the implications for businesses focused on physical products. As these digital natives prioritize experiences over material goods, traditional 'stuff' companies face significant challenges and must innovate to remain relevant.

KEY THEMES
• The rise of Native Digitals — A new generation that prioritizes digital experiences over physical goods.
• Economic impact — The shift away from material goods threatens industries reliant on physical products.
• Digital transformation — Companies must adapt by integrating digital products and services.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Native Digitals, primarily Millennials and Gen Z, are more interested in digital experiences than physical products.
• Insight 2: 74% of Americans now value experiences over physical products, reflecting a significant cultural shift.
• Insight 3: Economic constraints, such as housing affordability, contribute to the reduced desire for physical goods among younger generations.
• Insight 4: The trend towards digital life is causing a decline in demand for traditional 'stuff,' impacting GDP.
• Insight 5: Companies must innovate by offering digital products, services, and experiences to stay competitive.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Native Digitals — A generation whose primary life experience is digital.
• Experience Economy — A concept by Joe Pine that emphasizes the value of experiences over physical goods.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Native Digital people under 35 will progressively spend more time, money, and energy enhancing their lives through digital experiences."
"If your company is in the 'stuff' business, you might be in a bit of trouble."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Companies should innovate by integrating digital products and services alongside their physical offerings.
→ Businesses must recognize and adapt to the macro trend of digital prioritization to remain relevant.

name: The basics of MQLs
summary: Given the amount of things we need to focus on, we need to aim to be as efficient as possible in all of our business operations. This includes in our sales & marketing processes. As such, we need to shift our mindset to generate "Marketing Qualified Leads" (MQLs) rather than "generic" leads. An MQL is basically a potential customer that enters our sales pipeline with higher chances of converting, based on the the fact that it has demonstrated some form of intent towards doing business with us.

name: Triggers: The secret ingredient to drive purchases
summary:
Louis Grenier expains why we need to find out the triggers behind a customer´s decision to buy and how we can do it.
A "desire" is not enough for a customer to take action; in fact, we need to understand the constraints and the triggers to complete the scope of the decision to buy.

name: Going back to the fundamentals of Marketing
summary: In general, there are two "poles" to approach the role of marketing: the brand approach vs the data driven approach. In this episode they cover how marketing is going back to the fundamentals and the review some of the most important concepts

name: Overview of Crossfit´s business w/ CEO Eric Roza
summary:
In this episode, Eric Roza, CEO of CrossFit, discusses his strategic vision for the company, focusing on technology integration, expanding the CrossFit Games, and new business initiatives in eCommerce and healthcare. He also shares the challenges of revitalizing the brand and the unique circumstances that led to his acquisition of CrossFit.

KEY THEMES
• Technology in Fitness — Exploring the role of technology in CrossFit's future.
• Brand Revitalization — Strategies for overcoming challenges and turning around the CrossFit brand.
• Business Expansion — Initiatives in eCommerce, direct-to-consumer content, and healthcare.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Eric Roza envisions technology playing a crucial role in CrossFit's future growth.
• Insight 2: Expanding the CrossFit Games is a key component of the company's strategy.
• Insight 3: CrossFit is launching new initiatives in eCommerce and direct-to-consumer fitness content.
• Insight 4: Healthcare is becoming an integral part of CrossFit's business model.
• Insight 5: Eric Roza's acquisition of CrossFit was facilitated by a cold email and handshake deal.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Direct-to-Consumer Fitness Content — Delivering fitness content directly to consumers as a business strategy.
• CrossFit Games Expansion — Growing the competitive aspect of CrossFit to enhance brand visibility.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Eric Roza: 'Technology will be a cornerstone of CrossFit's future.'"
"Eric Roza: 'A cold email and handshake deal led to my acquisition of CrossFit.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore integrating more technology into fitness offerings to stay competitive.
→ Consider expanding competitive events to increase brand engagement and visibility.

name: Why you need to create an environment where it is safe for people to speak up
summary: Enabling such a culture helps identify mistakes, correct them, and empower people to be better

name: Peloton going into the virtual fitness space
summary:
This episode discusses Peloton's latest venture into the virtual fitness space with the introduction of an in-app video game called 'Lanebreak.' This move signifies Peloton's expansion of its content offerings and highlights a growing trend of integrating gaming with fitness equipment, a strategy also adopted by other companies like Ergatta.

KEY THEMES
• Integration of gaming and fitness — Peloton's new video game feature represents a blending of exercise with interactive entertainment.
• Expansion of content offerings — Peloton continues to diversify its content to enhance user engagement.
• Industry trends in connected fitness — Other companies, such as Ergatta, are also exploring the use of gaming in fitness equipment.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Peloton is launching a new video game called 'Lanebreak' for its bike users.
• Insight 2: The game allows users to control a wheel through a course by pedaling.
• Insight 3: Users can choose the music they listen to while playing the game.
• Insight 4: Peloton's move into gaming is part of a broader trend in the fitness industry.
• Insight 5: Ergatta, a competitor, has successfully integrated gaming with its rowing machines.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Connected fitness gaming — The concept of using fitness equipment as a gaming controller to enhance user engagement.
• Content diversification strategy — Peloton's approach to broadening its content offerings to attract and retain users.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Peloton has a new way to get your heart pumping: The connected bike maker is rolling out an in-app video game."
"The move further broadens Peloton’s suite of content."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore integrating gaming elements into fitness products to increase user engagement.
→ Consider diversifying content offerings to appeal to a broader audience in the fitness industry.

name: Customer personas in a post pandemic world
summary:
This episode explores the lasting impact of pandemic-induced consumer personas on the market, the challenges brands face in identifying their customers, and the permanent shifts in consumer behavior. It also covers future shopping trends, including in-store virtual reality experiences and Apple's new 'buy now, pay later' service, with insights from eMarketer principal analyst Suzy Davidkhanian.

KEY THEMES
• Pandemic Personas — Exploration of which consumer personas developed during the pandemic will persist.
• Consumer Behavior Changes — Discussion on permanent shifts in how consumers behave post-pandemic.
• Future Shopping Trends — Insights into how shopping experiences might evolve with new technologies and services.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Brands are struggling to identify their customers due to the shifts in consumer behavior caused by the pandemic.
• Insight 2: Some pandemic-induced consumer personas are expected to remain even as businesses fully reopen.
• Insight 3: In-store virtual reality experiences are emerging as a new trend in retail.
• Insight 4: Apple's 'buy now, pay later' service could significantly impact consumer purchasing behavior.
• Insight 5: Consumer behavior has likely changed permanently in several key ways due to the pandemic.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Pandemic Personas — Consumer personas that developed during the pandemic and their potential longevity.
• Buy Now, Pay Later — A service model that allows consumers to purchase products and pay for them over time.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Brands are struggling to know who their customers are in a post-pandemic world."
"Consumer behavior has likely changed permanently in several key ways."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Brands should reassess their customer personas to align with post-pandemic consumer behavior.
→ Consider integrating virtual reality experiences in-store to enhance customer engagement.

name: Maximize conversions with the traffic you have
summary: They review 3 things you can do to maximize conversions on your site: 1. Focus on page load speed 2. Social proof 3. Optimize your sales funnel

name: Focus on your core fitness business before diversifying into digital
summary:
helps a "brick & mortar" kickboxing brand owner determine if she should branch out into digital despite her amazing success in the traditional model. He provides three arguments
1.	From a capacity point of view, there is no need as she still has room to grow in the "brick & mortar" space.
2.	From an operations perspective, the grass is not always greener on the other side. Going digital implies a new set of skills, business model, challenges, which all go against her ability to focus on her core business.
3.	But, from the customer´s angle, it might make sense to test out if the user wants a "hybrid" experience and if they do, that might will be enough to prove the opportunity. But he advises her to test the concept first rather than going all in investing in production capabilities, marketing campaigns, etc. He suggest testing out the model in a few clubs, and go from there.

name: State of the industry & sport tech investments
summary:
This episode explores the intersection of sports and technology, highlighting innovative projects and investments in the sports industry. It features insights from leaders in sports tech, discussing the integration of AI, data analytics, and digital engagement strategies to enhance fan experiences and operational efficiencies.

KEY THEMES
• Sports Technology Innovation — The episode discusses how technology is revolutionizing sports through AI, data analytics, and digital platforms.
• Fan Engagement Strategies — Exploring new ways to captivate and retain sports fans using immersive and interactive technologies.
• Investment in Sports Tech — Highlighting the importance of strategic investments in emerging sports technologies to drive growth and engagement.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Tennis Australia's Beyond Tennis app combines AI, social media, and storytelling to engage fans.
• Insight 2: Ridley Plummer's work at Tennis Australia has positioned the Australian Open as a leader in Web3 and metaverse strategies.
• Insight 3: Peter's leadership at One Future Sports focuses on innovative sports technology and digital engagement.
• Insight 4: The Sports Innovation Summit serves as a platform for discussing challenges and opportunities in sports tech.
• Insight 5: The integration of AI in sports is enhancing analytics and performance insights for athletes and teams.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• AO ArtBall NFT — A project that uses NFTs to engage fans with the Australian Open.
• Fan Journey Model — A tool for mapping and enhancing the fan experience in sports venues.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Ridley Plummer: 'The Australian Open is pioneering Web3 and metaverse strategies.'"
"Peter: 'Innovation and impact are at the core of sports technology advancements.'"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Explore the use of AI and data analytics to enhance fan engagement and operational efficiency.
→ Consider investing in emerging sports technologies to stay ahead in the competitive sports industry.

name: Business masterclass for fitness business
summary:
Dan Martell gives awesome advice on this episode of the Growth Stacking Show to a crossfit gym owner on what he needs to focus on to grow his business. In essence, 3 questions to ask yourself:
•	What can you do to acquire more customers?
•	What can you do to keep them coming back?
•	What can you do to increase revenue per customer?
Every strategic decision you make from then on, should be based on those questions.

name: Lessons in Hospitality & Humanity
summary:
This episode of The Knowledge Project Podcast features Danny Meyer, a celebrated restaurateur, discussing the intersection of hospitality and humanity. Meyer shares insights on defining and delivering hospitality, scaling the feeling of hospitality, hiring practices, and maintaining a consistent value system amidst organizational growth. His experiences and philosophies are particularly relevant to anyone involved in service-oriented businesses.

KEY THEMES
• Hospitality and Humanity — Exploring the deep connection between delivering exceptional service and understanding human needs.
• Organizational Culture — The importance of maintaining core values while adapting cultural practices as a business grows.
• Leadership and Hiring — The significance of self-awareness in leadership and the art of identifying genuine candidates through non-verbal cues.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Hospitality is about believing that the person on the other side of the transaction is on your side.
• Insight 2: A consistent value system acts as a compass for organizational culture, which must evolve as the company grows.
• Insight 3: The ability to read 'kind eyes' is a critical skill in hiring, as it reflects a candidate's genuine emotional expression.
• Insight 4: Leaders should be self-aware and cautious of creating a cult-like environment that excludes diverse perspectives.
• Insight 5: Learning foreign languages opens up new worlds, similar to how scuba diving reveals a new dimension to swimmers.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Value System as Compass — A framework for ensuring organizational consistency amidst cultural change.
• Kind Eyes — A concept for assessing genuine emotional expression during the hiring process.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"Hospitality exists when you believe that the person on the other side of the transaction is on your side."
"You cannot lie in an interview if you don’t have kind eyes, because I can see that you have not been smiling for a good deal of your life."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate your organization's value system to ensure it remains a guiding compass as your culture evolves.
→ Develop the skill of reading non-verbal cues, such as 'kind eyes,' to improve hiring decisions.

name: Fitbit´s personalized emails as an example to engage your audience
summary:
It’s a good showcase of how to use personal data and community data in your emails to really build that one-to-one relationship with your audience and bring people back into your product
You can enjoy the analysis on written or video form but make sure to check it out, it provides great detail and examples to learn from!

name: Leveling up your "customer survey" game
summary:
Gathering customer feedback is critical for any business interested in iterating and adapting its product offering the actual needs of their consumers.
Customer surveys, although not as good of a method as actually seeing users interact with your services, are another form of doing gathering that feedback and as such, it should not be overlooked.

name: Learn "Cold emailing" from sales experts
summary:
This episode focuses on the art and science of cold emailing, featuring insights from sales experts across various companies. It discusses strategies for personalization, crafting engaging icebreakers, and avoiding spam filters, all aimed at improving email response rates and ultimately securing new business opportunities.

KEY THEMES
• Personalization in Cold Emails — Tailoring emails to the recipient's context and needs to increase engagement.
• Effective Email Structure — Crafting compelling icebreakers and smooth transitions to product pitches.
• Avoiding Spam Filters — Techniques to ensure emails reach the recipient's inbox.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The opening line of a cold email is crucial for capturing the recipient's attention and should be personalized and relevant.
• Insight 2: Transitioning from the icebreaker to the product pitch should involve connecting the recipient's needs with the solution offered.
• Insight 3: Avoiding spam involves both technical measures and ensuring the message is relevant and targeted to the right audience.
• Insight 4: Using humor and referencing recent events can be effective in engaging recipients, especially in specific industries like sports.
• Insight 5: Multi-channel outreach, including LinkedIn and phone calls, can complement email efforts and mitigate the risk of emails being marked as spam.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• ABCs of Outbound — A framework for crafting cold emails: Assess Your Who, Break Down Your What, Craft Your Why.
• Trigger-Based Outreach — Using specific actions or indicators as triggers to tailor and time outreach efforts.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""Your first sentence needs to intrigue readers to keep reading the rest of your email." — Filipe Brigas"
""Personalization only matters if it's relevant." — Will, Co-Founder of Lavender"

ACTION ITEMS
→ Experiment with different subject lines and opening lines to see what resonates best with your audience.
→ Use a mix of personalization and templated content to efficiently craft engaging emails without sacrificing relevance.

name: The difference between "Brand Identity" & "Branding"
summary:
This episode delves into the often misunderstood concepts of branding and brand identity, emphasizing their critical role in business success. It highlights the strategic importance of branding as an integral part of the business itself, rather than just a component, and discusses how effective branding can lead to customer loyalty and sustained growth.

KEY THEMES
• Branding as Business Essence — Branding should be seen as the core of the business, not just an aspect of it.
• Misconceptions about Branding — Many people confuse branding with its visual elements, overlooking its strategic importance.
• Emotional Connection and Customer Loyalty — Effective branding fosters emotional connections, leading to customer loyalty.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Branding is not just a part of a business; it is the business itself.
• Insight 2: Branding is often misunderstood as merely visual elements like logos and colors.
• Insight 3: A strong brand creates a powerful emotional connection with customers, enhancing loyalty.
• Insight 4: Retaining existing customers is more cost-effective than acquiring new ones, and branding plays a key role in retention.
• Insight 5: A unique brand identity can serve as a tool for sustained business growth.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Brand Identity — The intangible concept made of visual identity, personality, customer experience, and more.
• Brand Building — The process of creating a brand, often confused with just its visual aspects.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"A brand shouldn’t be seen and approached as part of a business. From a certain perspective, it is the business itself."
"Good branding is, in itself, an endless source of free advertising."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Invest in professional branding to ensure a strategic approach that aligns with business goals.
→ Focus on creating an emotional connection with customers to enhance loyalty and retention.

name: Seth Godin on Price vs Wants vs Needs
summary:
There are many ways to approach a "pricing decision" for a new product or service. Sometimes it is margin, others its brand positioning, and so on.
Truth is, we found this approach by Seth Godin simply awesome. It simplifies the decision to four quadrants defined by the following elements:
•	Price
•	The balance between "wants" & "needs.

name: A guide to audio marketing
summary:
This episode provides an update on the latest social media news, trends, and platform updates. It covers developments across various platforms like Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, and Facebook, highlighting new features and trends that marketers and brands should be aware of to stay competitive.

KEY THEMES
• Platform Innovation — New features and updates on platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn are shaping user engagement and marketing strategies.
• Generational Trends — Insights into Gen Z and millennial preferences are influencing brand strategies and marketing funnels.
• Influencer Marketing — The growing importance of influencer marketing, particularly on platforms like LinkedIn, is highlighted as a key strategy for brands.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Instagram is developing a feature called 'Blend' for a private feed of Reels shared between friends.
• Insight 2: Gen Z and millennials are significantly influenced by multicultural and diverse consumer representation in brands.
• Insight 3: LinkedIn is testing short-form video features, expanding its capabilities beyond networking and thought leadership.
• Insight 4: TikTok videos over 5 minutes have the highest average views, signaling a shift back to long-form content.
• Insight 5: The 50-plus market presents a significant opportunity for marketers, as highlighted by AdAge.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Search Value — A metric introduced in TikTok’s new creator monetization program to evaluate content.
• Friend Map — Instagram's upcoming feature allowing users to share live locations with friends.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"81% of Gen Z (and 72% of millennials) said that multicultural and diverse consumers have a significant impact on their brand preferences and choices."
"Gen Z doesn’t buy impulsively. They do their research first — whether it’s searching on TikTok or browsing reviews."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Marketers should explore influencer marketing opportunities on LinkedIn as it becomes a hub for brand-influencer collaborations.
→ Brands should consider targeting the 50-plus demographic, which remains an underutilized market segment.

name: Nielsen Webinar: The Changing Value of Sponsorship: 2021 Global Trends
summary:
Nielsen returns yet again with another webinar "Sport Sponsorship" focused webinar. This week, they discussed the Sales Impact as a Standard Metric vs traditional metrics like awareness or exposure.
From our point of view, the most relevant ideas were:
•	There is an increasing pressure for brands to demonstrate the value of a sponsorship and the sales it is driving (ROI).
•	New sponsorship models are emerging (Regional, performance related, short term focused on a particular product launch, split by channel, etc.)
•	The short term impact on sales (years 1-2), implies, more or less, an average of 1% increment on sales.
•	The long term impact on sales (up to 4-5 years), can drive an additional 2% increment on sales.
•	Predictions on further change
o	The value of the sponsorship will depend on the capacity to generate sales
o	Sales, acquisition and retention related metrics will replace vanity metrics (Likes, for example)
o	Ability to compare sponsorship activations to other promotional activities

name: Leadership lessons from Adam Mosseri (Head of Instagram)
summary:
Mosseri shares his thoughts on the evolution of the platform, how to hire new team members and lead them and he even inquires about leadership from NBA players.
He takes on the tough questions without hesitation and he provides fantastic lessons we believe you will appreciate! And we simply could not agree more with the quote he left at the end of the episode:
One of the most important things is to be honest with yourself with what matters to you most and then make sure you shape your time to align with your aspirations.

name: Remarkable lessons from a Women´s Soccer Legend
summary:
What stands out to us is the conversation around "the mistake" & "the redemption" in a series of events that happened during a World Cup Quaterfinals game against Germany. If you have followed sport for a while now, you might recognize this image...
Brandi shares the powerful lessons she learned about leadership and teamwork from those events and then they touch upon many other aspects (women empowerment, speaking up to your beliefs, choosing oneself, etc.) that we are pretty sure you will get a ton of value from!

name: Seth Godin on hockey helmets & changing the culture
summary:
a masterclass on what it takes to change the culture, sticking to your beliefs and pushing through the resistance around you using an example from the Major Hockey League.
Specifically, he discusses what it took and how long it took for helmets to be mandatory in the sport. We really enjoyed the following idea, which he shares towards the end of his rant:
Embrace the opportunity of changing the culture around you and look to normalize behaviors that will benefit all of us.
This is an awesome lesson to apply in both business & life!

name: "Hunger, Speed & Humility:" Traits that investors look for when evaluating entrepreneurs
summary:
The Masters of Scale podcast returns with another fantastic episode as they interview Mark Cuban on the traits that investors look for in entrepreneurs:
•	Hunger
•	Speed
•	Humility
They actually link to several examples from Cuban´s career or even some of the businesses he has been involved through Shark Tank.

name: The Pratfall Effect & the value of admitting flaws to generate trust
summary:
In a world that seems to value perfection (the perfect business idea, the perfect Instagram post, the perfect car, and so on...) there is value in actually admitting not being perfect.
This is the topic that another awesome episode of the "Everyone Hates Marketers" podcasts discusses this week. Louis Grenier explains The Pratfall Effect, which essentially explains: "If you admit a weakness, exhibit flaws, you become more appealing." As you will listen in the episode, this also translates into the business word as the intent to purchase is higher in brands that have high ratings but not perfect 5 star reviews.

name: Learning to rethink bad decisions
summary:
Can you count the number of bad decisions you have made in your life? A bad business decision, a project you should not have push forward that much, a personal investment or even relationship that you should have ended way beforehand (friendship, romantic relationship, etc.).
But out of those, looking back, how many of them do you wish you would have "pulled the plug" sooner in order to reduce the final impact it ended up causing?
This effect is what is commonly known as "Escalation of Commitment," and in this awesome episode of Worklife, Adam Grant covers why this happens and how we can reduce the chances of being impacted by it.
This topic is very relevant across all aspects of life and in the episode they even provide examples from NBA coaches, so be sure to check it out!

name: A perspective on the role of tech in the future of sport
summary:
"If you are not innovating, you are actually falling behind, not remaining still."
Jean Baptiste XXX; who was responsible for developing innovation strategy at UEFA & developing the UEFA innovation hub, shares the role, business and initiatives he was able to support through those vehicles.
Towards the end of the episode, he gives a small prediction on tech initiatives that could have most impact on sport in the future, so be sure to check it out!

name: Digital & virtual revenue in the fitness industry
summary:
The main ideas we got from the episode were:
•	Virtual & traditional models will complement each other: Both are here to stay
•	The necessity of traditional operators to consider developing a virtual offering will depend on each club´s members. This means that they should not create virtual offerings just for the sake of it. If this is something members could potentially value, then they should explore it.
•	The advantage of digital fitness services is that they enable brands to reach new customers that were not in the gym before. Even those who have not been "gym customers" at all...
•	Moreover, since local gyms are more "local-community" based, they have more potential to engage with local customers than "global-distant" big brands.
•	It is also a good tool to motivate and empower your employees. In fact, they are critical to make it all work...

name: The 3 most important factors to improve your marketing efforts
summary:
The Hirsh team shares the 3 most important factors that, if worked upon correctly can help you do so:
•	Creative & copywriting
•	Targetting
•	The offer
Those are three factors you can have direct influence on but at the end of the day, we fully agree with this quote shared at the beginning of the episode:
Marketing is a continuous process of testing, refining, and repeating that process.

name: Understanding Instagram´s "Reel Remix"
summary:
Instagram recently launched its "Instagram Reels Remixes" feature, in which users can now reply and create their own version of any reel on the platform.
We believe this could have huge potential for sport or fitness businesses. Why? Well, imagine your fans creating their own version of a player´s epic celebration. Or, users performing some version of the workout you just shared.

name: Basic review of how the algorithm for Facebook, Instagram & Twitter works
summary:
In today´s day & age, with so much content that is being put out in the world, it is extremely difficult to get a relevant place in the user´s news feed. The article focuses on how Facebook, Instagram & Twitter work but at the end of the day, it all comes down to one thing:
Making sure your content is of high quality, engaging and makes users come back to your profile. If you achieve that (much easier said than done), you should be good to go...

name: Facebook vs Google advertising
summary:
...It could be that you want to level up your Facebook marketing but that the marketing budget is under constraint at the moment and you end up having to choose between advertising on Facebook or Google.
Which one should you choose?
As always, it depends on many factors (your goal, who you are trying to reach, etc.) but perhaps this Hubspot article can be of help to let you make a decision. It basically compares the two platforms in terms of objectives, budget, etc.

name: Improve you website´s bounce rate
summary:
In this episode of Whiteboard Friday, Cyrus Shepard discusses the concept of bounce rate and its implications for SEO. He provides seven practical tips to reduce bounce rate by enhancing user engagement and satisfaction, which can indirectly benefit SEO performance.

KEY THEMES
• Bounce Rate — Understanding and addressing bounce rate as a proxy for user engagement and satisfaction.
• SEO Engagement Signals — The role of user engagement signals in SEO and how they relate to bounce rate.
• User Experience — Improving user experience through site speed, content relevance, and intuitive navigation.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Bounce rate is not a direct Google ranking signal, but it can serve as a proxy for user engagement and satisfaction.
• Insight 2: Improving page speed is a crucial factor in reducing bounce rate and enhancing user experience.
• Insight 3: Satisfying user intent broadly and deeply can lower bounce rate and improve engagement.
• Insight 4: Smart CTAs that incorporate ranking keywords can significantly enhance user interaction.
• Insight 5: Using an inverted pyramid style of writing can engage users more effectively by presenting key information upfront.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Inverted Pyramid Style — A writing technique from journalism that presents the most important information first to engage readers.
• Rage Clicks and Dead Clicks — Identifying and fixing non-functional elements on a website to improve user interaction.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"The goal is to increase engagement and to increase satisfaction, to make your users happier."
"Including your keywords in the CTAs is a very smart way and simple way of improving engagement and lowering your bounce rate."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Improve your website's page speed to enhance user experience and reduce bounce rate.
→ Conduct deep competitive analysis to ensure your content satisfies user intent effectively.

name: "Level up" your Facebook marketing game
summary:
Let´s begin though, by making sure that you are sure that your target market is on Facebook. If they are, then it makes sense to try out the new features and methods to engage with customers that social media platforms make available.
One such example is Facebook stories and if you haven´t gotten your head around how to use it just yet, this Hubspot article could be a good place to start.
Another tool launched by Facebook is its "automated ads" feature. The team at Ad Espresso developed this fantastic guide with screenshots, examples and overall great detail about how to use it. Given it is fueled by AI, it looks to make advertising process much more efficient and save your sport or fitness business time that you can spend on other areas.

name: 10 psychology concepts you need to know about to obtain more leads
summary:
This episode explores ten psychological concepts crucial for generating more leads in marketing. It emphasizes the importance of understanding consumer behavior and leveraging psychological insights to enhance marketing strategies and improve lead acquisition.

KEY THEMES
• Psychological Influence — Understanding how psychological principles can impact consumer behavior and decision-making.
• Lead Generation — Strategies to effectively attract and convert potential customers.
• Consumer Behavior — Insights into how consumers think and act, and how this can be used in marketing.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Psychological principles can significantly influence consumer decision-making and lead generation.
• Insight 2: Understanding consumer behavior is key to crafting effective marketing strategies.
• Insight 3: Leveraging psychological concepts can enhance the authenticity and appeal of marketing content.
• Insight 4: Content governance plays a critical role in maintaining brand identity in the zero-click era.
• Insight 5: AI is reshaping content and marketing roles, highlighting the need for adaptable strategies.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Content Governance — A strategy to maintain brand identity and authenticity in the age of AI-driven search.
• The CRISP Framework — A method to prepare content for AI interactions, ensuring clarity and relevance.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"AI engines are the new gatekeepers to your brand."
"Content governance is one of the biggest tools to ensure they reveal the brand identity you’ve created."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Implement content governance strategies to maintain brand authenticity.
→ Utilize psychological insights to enhance lead generation and consumer engagement.

name: Becoming "Age-Agnostic" & Achieving Omnipresence
summary:
This episode discusses the shift in marketing strategies necessitated by the pandemic, emphasizing the importance of omnichannel marketing and age-agnostic approaches. It highlights the need for brands to connect seamlessly across platforms and audiences, particularly as the global population ages and consumer digital penetration accelerates.

KEY THEMES
• Omnichannel Marketing — The necessity for brands to integrate their messaging across multiple platforms and channels.
• Age-Agnostic Marketing — Moving beyond targeting specific age groups to focus on shared consumer experiences.
• Digital Transformation — The accelerated shift towards digital engagement and e-commerce due to the pandemic.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: The pandemic has accelerated the need for omnichannel marketing, pushing brands to transcend physical and audience barriers.
• Insight 2: Brands must target both digital natives and digital immigrants, as the global consumer base is aging.
• Insight 3: Companies like Microsoft and BT are leading the way by focusing on technology adoption rather than age demographics.
• Insight 4: The pandemic has increased digital engagement among Gen X and boomers, with significant growth in mobile platform use.
• Insight 5: Omnichannel experiences, like the Starbucks rewards app, are essential for maintaining consistent customer engagement.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Omnichannel Marketing — A strategy that integrates various marketing channels to provide a seamless customer experience.
• Age-Agnostic Marketing — An approach that targets consumers based on shared experiences rather than age demographics.

NOTABLE QUOTES
""The pandemic has wiped its germy hands over every marketing strategy and incinerated the rule books.""
""Brands must become age-agnostic, aiming instead to unite consumers through their lived experiences.""

ACTION ITEMS
→ Brands should develop omnichannel strategies that integrate digital and physical customer experiences.
→ Marketers should adopt an age-agnostic approach, focusing on shared consumer experiences rather than age demographics.

name: Sport business lessons from Ted Leonsis´s career
summary: In this article, Sportico reviews Ted Leonsis´ (Owner at Monumental Sports & Enterntainment) career and different landmark events such as the purchase of the Washington Wizards and other Washington-based sport properties, including their eSports team, their pivot into digital (and looking like a SaaS company), drafting international players or the upcoming technologies that will impact sport.

name: eMarketer´s take on the NFL´s & Amazon broadcasting deal
summary: very useful in case you want to understand the state of the sports broadcasting industry after Amazon´s deal with the NFL. Is this the future of broadcasting? Are users adapting to new ways of consuming sports? Are traditional TV broadcasters at risk? These, and more topics are discussed, with many supporting facts in pure eMarketer style...so don´t miss it

name: Want to have engaged users? Then make sure you treat your employees well..
summary:
Make sure you treat your employees well, show empathy towards the challenges they face on a daily basis and are engaged with the overall strategy of the business.
It may seem basic / obvious but not all businesses do this. At the end of the day, your personnel has more touchpoints with the customers than executives. If they "feel the brand," chances are they will deliver a better customer experience that those who do not.
They also discuss tools, tactics and many other topics that may give you ideas you can implement in your business!

name: Creating Long vs Short term content strategies to drive higher ROI
summary:
you will learn, both from a strategic and tactical point of view, how to develop a content marketing strategy that balances the long and the short term point of view to drive a higher ROI.
Some marketers rely purely on keyword research, others only on "what they know," but at the end of the day, we need to find out what content makes our "content" stick, develop it and make sure we put the proper processes in place to test out our content and find out what works best.
As it is mentioned in the episode, marketers do not need more brilliant ideas, but rather processes and operations that are effective in teaching us what our customers (or potential customers) value...

name: Communication & sticking to results before methods
summary:
This episode of Business for Unicorns features Jean-Claude Vacassin, the Founding Director of W10 Performance, discussing the importance of communication and focusing on results before methods in business. The conversation highlights insights from Jean-Claude's experience in the fitness industry and his work with corporate wellbeing programs, offering valuable advice for entrepreneurs and business leaders.

KEY THEMES
• Communication — The critical role of effective communication in business success.
• Results over Methods — Prioritizing outcomes rather than getting bogged down in specific processes.
• Corporate Wellbeing — Integrating wellness programs into corporate culture for enhanced performance.

MAIN INSIGHTS
• Insight 1: Effective communication is a cornerstone of successful business operations.
• Insight 2: Focusing on results rather than methods can lead to more innovative and effective solutions.
• Insight 3: Corporate wellbeing programs can significantly improve employee performance and satisfaction.
• Insight 4: The fitness industry offers unique insights into managing teams and client relationships.
• Insight 5: Entrepreneurs can benefit from adopting a results-oriented mindset in their strategic planning.

FRAMEWORKS & CONCEPTS
• Results Before Methods — A business approach that emphasizes achieving desired outcomes over adhering to specific processes.

NOTABLE QUOTES
"A business can make money while improving the lives of their employees and customers."
"Communication is the key to unlocking the potential of any team."

ACTION ITEMS
→ Evaluate your current communication strategies and identify areas for improvement.
→ Shift focus from rigid processes to flexible, results-oriented strategies in your business planning.

name: What can your sport business learn from Chris Paul´s transition to a plant based diet?
summary:
In another awesome episode of "Masters of Scale," Reid Hoffman tries to explain a powerful idea to ponder whenever you try to launch a new product or service:
"I believe that you need to listen to your customers ... even when what they want is inconvenient, or inconsistent. But you must track their point of view … and let them know you're listening."
He uses the marketing process that Ethan Brown, founder & CEO of Beyond Meat, followed to launch the product into the market.
He also compares this to how NBA Legend, Chris Paul, approached his training staff when he decided to transition to a "plant-based" diet even though they were, at the beginning, sceptickal about his decision.
People, customers among them, sometimes do now know what they want, but the challenge is to listen to them and adapt our communication strategies to address the "pains" (with regards to a particular product category) they are experiencing.

name: Learning to sell on YouTube to grow your business
summary:
The discussion, which goes into awesome detail with real examples, is centered around 3 key ideas:
•	How to avoid the biggest mistakes
•	Selling on YouTube using "soft pitches"
•	How to do a "hard ask" on the platform
YouTube is a platform that can pretty much work for any business but in our opinion, for those with a sport or fitness business, should definitely consider including it as a key channel of the content marketing strategy...so don´t miss it!

name: Liteboxer: Review from their CMO
summary: Vanessa Severiano interviews Liteboxer´s CMO and they cover topics such as the opportunity for the brand, challenges, hiring and retaining talent, the competition. We particularly liked the way she believes brands compete in the market. This is based on market differentiation, communication channels and innovation

name: Unlocking the power of influencer marketing
summary: Every marketing strategy revolves around the idea of influencing people to perform an action. Hence, everything is a form of influencer marketing. This episode goes deep into that concept and how your brand can unlock the true potential of influences marketing.

name: Product Positioning and the Product Marketing Partnership
summary: Interesting differentiation between product positioning (long term) vs product marketing (short term). Also nice to remember the brand marketing pyramid: Functional / Logical / Emotional benefits

name: Different ways to calculate "Conversion Rates"
summary: Understanding conversion rates is a critical element (although not the only one) to determine the effectiveness of your marketing campaigns. However, it is a metric that will vary based on the context. Learn the different methods to calculate it.

name: Detailed Guide to understand "Content Strategy"
summary:
This episode provides a comprehensive guide to understanding content strategy, emphasizing its role in achieving specific marketing goals through content creation, promotion, and measurement. It highlights the importance of audience insights, content mission statements, and the integration of SEO and influencer marketing to build a successful content strategy.

KEY THEMES
• Content Strategy Basics — Understanding content strategy as a plan to use content to achieve marketing goals.
• Audience Insights — The importance of knowing your audience to create resonant content.
